32:15.ar: إِنَّمَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهَا خَرُّواْۤ سُجَّدࣰ اۤ وَسَبَّحُواْ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ۩
32:15.en: Only those believe in Our revelations who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrate and hymn the praise of their Lord, and they are not scornful

32:16.ar: تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّهُمۡ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
32:16.en: Who forsake their beds to cry unto their Lord in fear and hope, and spend of that We have bestowed on them

32:17.ar: فَلَا تَعۡلَمُ نَفۡسࣱ مَّآ أُخۡفِيَ لَهُم مِّن قُرَّةِ أَعۡيُنࣲ جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
32:17.en: No soul knoweth what is kept hid for them of joy, as a reward for what they used to do

32:18.ar: أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقࣰ اۚ لَّا يَسۡتَوُۥنَ
32:18.en: Is he who is a believer like unto him who is an evil-liver? They are not alike

32:19.ar: أَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتُ ٱلۡمَأۡوَىٰ نُزُلَۢا بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
32:19.en: But as for those who believe and do good works, for them are the Gardens of Retreat - a welcome (in reward) for what they used to do

32:20.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فَسَقُواْ فَمَأۡوَىٰهُمُ ٱلنَّارُۖ كُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓاْ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَآ أُعِيدُواْ فِيهَا وَقِيلَ لَهُمۡ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ
32:20.en: And as for those who do evil, their retreat is the Fire. Whenever they desire to issue forth from thence, they are brought back thither. Unto them it is said: Taste the torment of the Fire which ye used to deny

32:21.ar: وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ دُونَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَكۡبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
32:21.en: And verily We make them taste the lower punishment before the greater, that haply they may return

32:22.ar: وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن ذُكِّرَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ ثُمَّ أَعۡرَضَ عَنۡهَآۚ إِنَّا مِنَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُنتَقِمُونَ
32:22.en: And who doth greater wrong than he who is reminded of the revelations of his Lord, then turneth from them. Lo! We shall requite the guilty

32:23.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ فَلَا تَكُن فِي مِرۡيَةࣲ مِّن لِّقَآئِهِۦۖ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ هُدࣰ ى لِّبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ
32:23.en: We verily gave Moses the Scripture; so be not ye in doubt of his receiving it; and We appointed it a guidance for the Children of Israel

32:24.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡ أَئِمَّةࣰ يَهۡدُونَ بِأَمۡرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُواْۖ وَكَانُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يُوقِنُونَ
32:24.en: And when they became steadfast and believed firmly in Our revelations, We appointed from among them leaders who guided by Our command

32:25.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ يَفۡصِلُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ فِيمَا كَانُواْ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَ
32:25.en: Lo! thy Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ

32:2.ar: تَنزِيلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهِ مِن رَّبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
32:2.en: The revelation of the Scripture whereof there is no doubt is from the Lord of the Worlds

32:3.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ ٱفۡتَرَىٰهُۚ بَلۡ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أَتَىٰهُم مِّن نَّذِيرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَهۡتَدُونَ
32:3.en: Or say they: He hath invented it? Nay, but it is the Truth from thy Lord, that thou mayst warn a folk to whom no warner came before thee, that haply they may walk aright

32:4.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ مَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ مِن وَلِيࣲّ وَلَا شَفِيعٍۚ أَفَلَا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ
32:4.en: Allah it is Who created the heavens and the earth, and that which is between them, in six Days. Then He mounted the Throne. Ye have not, beside Him, a protecting friend or mediator. Will ye not then remember

32:5.ar: يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ثُمَّ يَعۡرُجُ إِلَيۡهِ فِي يَوۡمࣲ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُۥٓ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ
32:5.en: He directeth the ordinance from the heaven unto the earth; then it ascendeth unto Him in a Day, whereof the measure is a thousand years of that ye reckon

32:6.ar: ذَٰلِكَ عَٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
32:6.en: Such is the Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, the Mighty, the Merciful

32:7.ar: ٱلَّذِيٓ أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ خَلَقَهُۥۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلۡقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ مِن طِينࣲ‏
32:7.en: Who made all things good which He created, and He began the creation of man from clay

32:8.ar: ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسۡلَهُۥ مِن سُلَٰلَةࣲ مِّن مَّآءࣲ مَّهِينࣲ‏
32:8.en: Then He made his seed from a draught of despised fluid

32:9.ar: ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِۦۖ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَ وَٱلۡأَفۡـِٔدَةَۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَشۡكُرُونَ
32:9.en: Then He fashioned him and breathed into him of His Spirit; and appointed for you hearing and sight and hearts. Small thanks give ye

32:10.ar: وَقَالُوٓاْ أَءِذَا ضَلَلۡنَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَءِنَّا لَفِي خَلۡقࣲ جَدِيدِۭۚ بَلۡ هُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّهِمۡ كَٰفِرُونَ
32:10.en: And they say: When we are lost in the earth, how can we then be re-created? Nay but they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord

32:11.ar: ۞قُلۡ يَتَوَفَّىٰكُم مَّلَكُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ ٱلَّذِي وُكِّلَ بِكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ تُرۡجَعُونَ
32:11.en: Say: The angel of death, who hath charge concerning you, will gather you, and afterward unto your Lord ye will be returned

32:12.ar: وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ نَاكِسُواْ رُءُوسِهِمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ رَبَّنَآ أَبۡصَرۡنَا وَسَمِعۡنَا فَٱرۡجِعۡنَا نَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحًا إِنَّا مُوقِنُونَ
32:12.en: Couldst thou but see when the guilty hang their heads before their Lord, (and say): Our Lord! We have now seen and heard, so send us back; we will do right, now we are sure

32:13.ar: وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَأٓتَيۡنَا كُلَّ نَفۡسٍ هُدَىٰهَا وَلَٰكِنۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ مِنِّي لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ
32:13.en: And if We had so willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me concerning evildoers took effect: that I will fill hell with the jinn and mankind together

4:49.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُمۚ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشَآءُ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا
4:49.en: Hast thou not seen those who praise themselves for purity? Nay, Allah purifieth whom He will, and they will not be wronged even the hair upon a date-stone

57:16.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ يَأۡنِ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَن تَخۡشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمۡ لِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا نَزَلَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَطَالَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَمَدُ فَقَسَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡۖ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
57:16.en: Is not the time ripe for the hearts of those who believe to submit to Allah's reminder and to the truth which is revealed, that they become not as those who received the scripture of old but the term was prolonged for them and so their hearts were hardened, and many of them are evil-livers

57:17.ar: ٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحۡيِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَاۚ قَدۡ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
57:17.en: Know that Allah quickeneth the earth after its death. We have made clear Our revelations for you, that haply ye may understand

33:69.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ ءَاذَوۡاْ مُوسَىٰ فَبَرَّأَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِمَّا قَالُواْۚ وَكَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَجِيهࣰ ا
33:69.en: O ye who believe! Be not as those who slandered Moses, but Allah proved his innocence of that which they alleged, and he was well esteemed in Allah's sight

11:96.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَسُلۡطَٰنࣲ مُّبِينٍ
11:96.en: And verily We sent Moses with Our revelations and a clear warrant

11:97.ar: إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِۦ فَٱتَّبَعُوٓاْ أَمۡرَ فِرۡعَوۡنَۖ وَمَآ أَمۡرُ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِرَشِيدࣲ‏
11:97.en: Unto Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they did follow the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was no right guide

20:84.ar: قَالَ هُمۡ أُوْلَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِي وَعَجِلۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ رَبِّ لِتَرۡضَىٰ
20:84.en: He said: They are close upon my track. I hastened unto Thee, my Lord, that Thou mightest be well pleased

7:137.ar: وَأَوۡرَثۡنَا ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَانُواْ يُسۡتَضۡعَفُونَ مَشَٰرِقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَغَٰرِبَهَا ٱلَّتِي بَٰرَكۡنَا فِيهَاۖ وَتَمَّتۡ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُواْۖ وَدَمَّرۡنَا مَا كَانَ يَصۡنَعُ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَقَوۡمُهُۥ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡرِشُونَ
7:137.en: And We caused the folk who were despised to inherit the eastern parts of the land and the western parts thereof which We had blessed. And the fair word of thy Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their endurance; and We annihilated (all) that Pharaoh and his folk had done and that they had contrived

hVK2JB8vmR0.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat As-Sajdah (verses 15-25)
hVK2JB8vmR0.one_line: A living versus routine relationship with Allah, admitting the deficiency, the lover's night prayer, and why Musa, who spoke with Allah, appears at the surah's end.
hVK2JB8vmR0.summary: Reviewing the traits of true believers, he stresses that they erase their own sense of rank and that only a lover leaves his bed. Like a marriage that decays into bills and errands, worship can become a hated job done until retirement; Allah wants a servant who has absorbed everything the surah described. No one with an atom of arrogance enters paradise, so do not praise yourself. If you do not feel this longing, admit it, as a patient must accept a diagnosis before treatment, and do not despair: the verse that Allah revives dead earth is the most hopeful in the Quran for a hardened heart. Hardship is the lesser punishment meant to return you, which is why scholars worried when no trial came. Long night prayer like the Prophet's or Ibn Mas'ud's comes from enjoyment, not discipline alone, as people lose track of hours at games they love; but this love must be sought to be given. In verses 22-25, the most unjust is one who turns away when reminded. Musa is mentioned because Allah spoke to him directly, and the Prophet is told he will meet him; the patient and certain among his followers became imams. The deen is passed on orally through scholars who transmit their state before their knowledge.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: they deny themselves any rank
outline.gist: True believers fall in prostration and see no standing for themselves before Allah, which is real humility, not the claims of union with the divine.

outline.heading: Only a lover leaves his bed
outline.gist: Sides drawing away from beds describe someone who can think only of the beloved; hearts prostrate before foreheads do.

outline.heading: When a marriage turns to routine
outline.gist: Early longing fades over years; he recounts a couple who had lived seven years sharing only food, bills and children, with empty hearts.

outline.heading: Worship like a hated job
outline.gist: Speaking to Allah with a distracted heart, as if He had not rescued and blessed you, is like an employee doing the minimum while counting down to retirement.

outline.heading: The servant Allah wants
outline.gist: One who has truly absorbed each truth of the surah: the Book without doubt, creation, no intercessor, His knowledge and mercy, his own origin and return.

outline.heading: No one with an atom of arrogance enters paradise
outline.gist: Seeing yourself as better than any creature lets arrogance into the heart; a servant has no ups and downs of status.

outline.heading: Do not praise yourselves
outline.gist: Only Allah purifies whom He wills; you know neither your own ending nor another's rank with Him.

outline.heading: Admit what is missing
outline.gist: Do not fake feelings you lack, but acknowledge the lack, as a patient must accept a diagnosis; then ask what has kept your heart from loving Allah.

outline.heading: Is it not time for hearts to humble themselves?
outline.gist: The verse reached the companions early in Makkah and each asked the other what he had done to deserve it; do not let time harden your heart.

outline.heading: The most hopeful verse: He revives the dead earth
outline.gist: If Allah revives dead land, He can revive a heart that feels it cannot humble itself.

outline.heading: The lesser punishment, and scholars who feared its absence
outline.gist: Losses and illness are sent so we return; poor, devoted scholars worried that a period without trial meant Allah was leading them on.

outline.heading: Every hardship is a personal message
outline.gist: The oath in the verse explains all worldly calamity as part of your relationship with Allah, purifying faults and calling you back.

outline.heading: A heart emptied of all but Allah
outline.gist: When the heart holds only Allah, honouring parents, kinship and providing for children are done because He commanded them.

outline.heading: The Prophet's chest boiling like a pot
outline.gist: His suppressed weeping in prayer and reciting several long surahs in one rak'ah are the acts of a lover, not mere self-discipline.

outline.heading: Discipline versus enjoyment
outline.gist: Discipline gets you through a Ramadan khatm, but standing four or five hours is done only by one who enjoys it, as gamers and card players lose all sense of time; many early scholars finished the Quran in two rak'ahs.

outline.heading: Ibn Mas'ud nearly left the Prophet's prayer
outline.gist: He was tempted to sit down during the Prophet's long recitation, yet later finished the Quran in one to three nights, having learned love from the Prophet.

outline.heading: Ask for it to be given it
outline.gist: You must first notice the deficiency and then seek it; like an order you have to place, the gift of His love is not delivered unrequested.

outline.heading: Trials mean He still wants you back
outline.gist: The language of the hadith of the beloved is lovers' speech; if He tests you, He still loves you and seeks your heart's return.

outline.heading: Recitation of the closing passage
outline.gist: He reads the verses on those who turn away and on Musa and the Israelites.

outline.heading: Who is more unjust than one who turns away?
outline.gist: The same word 'reminded' sets him against the believers who fall in prostration: given everything, he refuses to listen.

outline.heading: Turning away from self-sufficiency or arrogance
outline.gist: One who turns away either thinks he does not need you or thinks you unworthy of his attention; hence the stern warning of retribution.

outline.heading: Musa appears briefly across the Quran
outline.gist: Short mentions of Musa at the ends of Al-Ahzab and Hud remind the Prophet to reflect.

outline.heading: Why Musa here: the one Allah spoke to directly
outline.gist: A relationship needs speech, and Musa alone was addressed without intermediary; revealed shortly before the Night Journey, the verse tells the Prophet not to doubt he will meet him.

outline.heading: Imagining the conversations of the Ascension
outline.gist: He likes to picture what the Prophet and the prophets discussed; Musa hastened to his Lord and lengthened his speech out of love of hearing Him.

outline.heading: Imams who guide by patience
outline.gist: As Musa was guidance for his people, the Prophet is our model in connecting with Allah; not all Israelites are blamed, and their good is always linked to patience.

outline.heading: Patience and certainty make leaders
outline.gist: Certainty echoes the surah's opening 'no doubt'; the Prophet understood that a model without love for Allah fails, so he kept praying at night as a grateful servant.

outline.heading: Allah will judge their disputes
outline.gist: Do not be absorbed by what became of later Israelites; look at Musa and those who followed him, and at the need for successors who carry the message.

outline.heading: The deen is taken from scholars, not books
outline.gist: Knowledge passed mouth to mouth from Jibril to the Prophet to each generation; renewal comes from scholars within the tradition, not from outsiders.

outline.heading: Transmitting a state of love
outline.gist: Scholars who stood against occupiers carried this chain; the Prophet passed on not only rulings but his love of Allah, generation after generation.

outline.heading: Outro

10:90.ar: ۞وَجَٰوَزۡنَا بِبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَتۡبَعَهُمۡ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ بَغۡيࣰ ا وَعَدۡوًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدۡرَكَهُ ٱلۡغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَامَنَتۡ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓاْ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
10:90.en: And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh with his hosts pursued them in rebellion and transgression, till, when the (fate of) drowning overtook him, he exclaimed: I believe that there is no Allah save Him in Whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of those who surrender (unto Him)

10:91.ar: ءَآلۡـَٰٔنَ وَقَدۡ عَصَيۡتَ قَبۡلُ وَكُنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ

10:92.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنۡ خَلۡفَكَ ءَايَةࣰۚ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا لَغَٰفِلُونَ
10:92.en: But this day We save thee in thy body that thou mayst be a portent for those after thee. Lo! most of mankind are heedless of Our portents

32:12.ar: وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ نَاكِسُواْ رُءُوسِهِمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ رَبَّنَآ أَبۡصَرۡنَا وَسَمِعۡنَا فَٱرۡجِعۡنَا نَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحًا إِنَّا مُوقِنُونَ
32:12.en: Couldst thou but see when the guilty hang their heads before their Lord, (and say): Our Lord! We have now seen and heard, so send us back; we will do right, now we are sure

32:14.ar: فَذُوقُواْ بِمَا نَسِيتُمۡ لِقَآءَ يَوۡمِكُمۡ هَٰذَآ إِنَّا نَسِينَٰكُمۡۖ وَذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
32:14.en: So taste (the evil of your deeds). Forasmuch as ye forgot the meeting of this your day, lo! We forget you. Taste the doom of immortality because of what ye used to do

37:16.ar: أَءِذَا مِتۡنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابࣰ ا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبۡعُوثُونَ

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا

PTwj0Dm4Vk0.title: Tazkiyah Halaqa: Mortality, Episode 30
PTwj0Dm4Vk0.one_line: Mortality gives life beauty, accountability gives it morality; once the book closes at death we lose control of our fate, so act now.
PTwj0Dm4Vk0.summary: He argues that mortality lets us see beauty and value the present, but on its own it can even argue against ethics; only accountability before Allah gives a reason to stay moral. Two last points close the mortality section: drop the need to be remembered, which also drives families into mourning innovations beyond Islam's three days, and remember that everyone dies exactly at their decreed time, so there is nothing to regret. Turning to accountability before Allah, distinct from self-accountability, he notes that we judge others instantly but hate being judged, and that without accountability no Islamic argument holds. In the grave the dead hear their loved ones walk away, and their prayer, fasting, charity and good deeds stand guard. Life is a series of choices recorded until death, when the book is sealed; like Pharaoh, late pleas no longer count, and the criminals' wish to be sent back is refused. Societies need laws with consequences, din itself means law, and only belief in later accountability explains how disadvantaged prophets and companions kept high ethical standards, unlike pre-Islamic Arabs who relied on reputation. He challenges listeners to test whether they truly believe in resurrection and judgment, and to use that belief to take charge of their lives while they still can.

outline.heading: Opening
Mortality and accountability go hand in hand
outline.gist: Accepting mortality includes accepting what follows it; mortality lets us enjoy life, accountability lets us have morality.

outline.heading: Nothing is built to last
outline.gist: Finitude is what makes life beautiful; even institutions obsess over building to last when they cannot fix today's problems.

outline.heading: Thinking big as escape
outline.gist: Long-term vision is good, but grand plans can be a way to avoid what is in front of you; morality needs accountability.

outline.heading: You can conclude morality but not defend it
outline.gist: Alone on an island you would reach honesty, kindness and loyalty, but could not argue why to keep them in a world ruled by the law of the jungle.

outline.heading: Mortality alone can argue against ethics
outline.gist: If you only live once and were dealt the upper hand, why not hold onto it at any cost? Accountability answers this.

outline.heading: The need to be remembered
outline.gist: Once you focus on a good ending and hope in Allah, the fear of mortality becomes motivation, but the wish to be remembered can still worsen it.

outline.heading: Put your affairs in order
outline.gist: Write your will, make amends and spend time with loved ones so no regrets remain; a need to be remembered leaves families feeling guilty.

outline.heading: Mourning innovations and the three-day limit
outline.gist: Fortieth-day and yearly rituals and delaying inheritance are not from Islam; mourning is three days, then life continues with good deeds for the deceased.

outline.heading: What matters is that Allah remembers you
outline.gist: Whether people remember you should not matter; let go of needing it.

outline.heading: You leave exactly at your decreed time
outline.gist: Your breaths were numbered from birth; whether by murder or error, nothing was missed, so there is nothing to regret for yourself or others.

outline.heading: No soul dies before its term
outline.gist: The Prophet said Jibril inspired into his heart that no soul dies until it completes what was decreed for it.

outline.heading: Accountability before Allah, not self-accountability
outline.gist: Earlier he taught holding oneself to account; this is being held to account by Allah, which the nafs dislikes.

outline.heading: We judge instantly but hate being judged
outline.gist: People accept judgment only in handcuffs before a court, yet automatically size up everyone who walks in.

outline.heading: Without accountability no argument holds
outline.gist: Remove resurrection and judgment from Islam or any ethical system and nothing can be argued any longer.

outline.heading: Hearing the footsteps walk away
outline.gist: The Quran's many terms for the Last Day point to one concept, and the Prophet said the buried hear people leaving.

outline.heading: Alone in the grave
outline.gist: Spouse, mother and children all leave, as they should after dua; understanding this loneliness lets you prepare so you are not alone.

outline.heading: Your deeds stand guard
outline.gist: Prayer sits at your head, fasting and charity at your sides and other good deeds at your feet, blocking punishment from every side.

outline.heading: Life is a series of recorded choices
outline.gist: Every moment you choose, and each choice is written and added up until death.

outline.heading: Last-moment faith may not count
outline.gist: Once death is too advanced, words may not count, as with Pharaoh's belief while drowning.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's body preserved as a sign
outline.gist: His body was kept as a lesson; despite some scholars' hopes, the verses are clear that his late faith did not count.

outline.heading: The book is sealed
outline.gist: The recording angel stops writing; the realisation that you can no longer affect your fate is deeply painful.

outline.heading: You control your fate now
outline.gist: Every decision now shifts your place on the Day of Judgment, so keep improving it while you can.

outline.heading: The criminals beg to be sent back
outline.gist: Heads bowed, they claim full certainty and ask to return to do right.

outline.heading: Forgotten as they forgot
outline.gist: They are told to taste the punishment; after death you are a sitting duck who can no longer make a difference.

outline.heading: Shift the worry to your choices
outline.gist: Concern moves from the moment of death to whether you are choosing rightly; morality needs a system of reward and punishment.

outline.heading: Governments only punish
outline.gist: States rarely reward lifelong service but destroy you for one mistake, and laws are what keep people from harming each other.

outline.heading: Lawlessness always becomes hell on earth
outline.gist: Nomadic groups bought protection with unjust rules; every attempt to remove law brought horrors against the weak, women, children and minorities.

outline.heading: Din means law
outline.gist: Prophets bring laws for this life and laws enforced in the next.

outline.heading: Laws fail unless people accept them
outline.gist: Strict laws and efficient enforcers fail if people do not hold themselves to them.

outline.heading: Man-made law follows the crowd
outline.gist: Cannabis was legalised and taxed once people ignored the ban; divine law exists to restrain collective desire and anchor right and wrong.

outline.heading: The disadvantaged and morality
outline.gist: Without belief in later accountability, it is nearly impossible to convince someone dealt a hard hand to act ethically.

outline.heading: Answering the atheist argument
outline.gist: Humans can conceive morality but cannot enforce it, while the persecuted prophets and companions kept high standards anyway.

outline.heading: Morality of convenience
outline.gist: The rich forbid theft and the weak forbid killing; someone with nothing to lose has no such reason.

outline.heading: Why the companions held firm
outline.gist: In Arabia the unprotected were preyed upon, yet the disadvantaged companions kept their ethics through certainty of being questioned by Allah.

outline.heading: Do you truly believe?
outline.gist: The Quran disputed only two things with the pagans, who already believed in God: shirk, and denial of resurrection.

outline.heading: Without resurrection morality is a suggestion
outline.gist: They mocked returning after turning to dust, so justice and self-control were mere recommendations.

outline.heading: Worshipping reputation: Hatim al-Ta'i
outline.gist: The pagans built ethics on reputation, as with Hatim slaughtering all his camels in one night to be remembered as generous; shame-driven ethics fail in the long run.

outline.heading: 'Yes, by my Lord, you will be raised'
outline.gist: The Quran answers their denial with an emphatic oath that they will be resurrected and told what they did.

outline.heading: Repeating creation is easier
outline.gist: He who began creation will repeat it, and even by human logic doing something a second time is easier.

outline.heading: Most people do not really believe
outline.gist: If billions truly believed they would recite their deeds before Allah, our problems would not be what they are.

outline.heading: Faces falling from shame
outline.gist: A great scholar wept that people's faces would fall from their bones in embarrassment when reciting their deeds to Allah.

outline.heading: Accountability makes mortality easy
outline.gist: Once you truly accept it, dying is no longer the problem; what matters is what is in your book and how you will explain it.

outline.heading: Belief in resurrection is essential to being Muslim
outline.gist: Removing either tawhid or the Last Day puts one among the pagans; many claim belief without its truth.

outline.heading: You still control your fate
outline.gist: Allah set things in your favour and has no wish to punish the grateful believer, so use accountability to take charge rather than despair.

outline.heading: Outro

32:26.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَهۡدِ لَهُمۡ كَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ يَمۡشُونَ فِي مَسَٰكِنِهِمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتٍۚ أَفَلَا يَسۡمَعُونَ
32:26.en: Is it not a guidance for them (to observe) how many generations We destroyed before them, amid whose dwelling places they do walk? Lo! therein verily are portents! Will they not then heed

32:27.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّا نَسُوقُ ٱلۡمَآءَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلۡجُرُزِ فَنُخۡرِجُ بِهِۦ زَرۡعࣰ ا تَأۡكُلُ مِنۡهُ أَنۡعَٰمُهُمۡ وَأَنفُسُهُمۡۚ أَفَلَا يُبۡصِرُونَ
32:27.en: Have they not seen how We lead the water to the barren land and therewith bring forth crops whereof their cattle eat, and they themselves? Will they not then see

32:28.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلۡفَتۡحُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
32:28.en: And they say: When cometh this victory (of yours) if ye are truthful

32:29.ar: قُلۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَتۡحِ لَا يَنفَعُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِيمَٰنُهُمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنظَرُونَ
32:29.en: Say (unto them): On the day of the victory the faith of those who disbelieve (and who then will believe) will not avail them, neither will they be reprieved

32:30.en: So withdraw from them (O Muhammad), and await (the event). Lo! they (also) are awaiting (it)

32:15.ar: إِنَّمَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهَا خَرُّواْۤ سُجَّدࣰ اۤ وَسَبَّحُواْ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ۩
32:15.en: Only those believe in Our revelations who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrate and hymn the praise of their Lord, and they are not scornful

32:16.ar: تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّهُمۡ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
32:16.en: Who forsake their beds to cry unto their Lord in fear and hope, and spend of that We have bestowed on them

32:17.ar: فَلَا تَعۡلَمُ نَفۡسࣱ مَّآ أُخۡفِيَ لَهُم مِّن قُرَّةِ أَعۡيُنࣲ جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
32:17.en: No soul knoweth what is kept hid for them of joy, as a reward for what they used to do

32:18.ar: أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقࣰ اۚ لَّا يَسۡتَوُۥنَ
32:18.en: Is he who is a believer like unto him who is an evil-liver? They are not alike

32:19.ar: أَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتُ ٱلۡمَأۡوَىٰ نُزُلَۢا بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
32:19.en: But as for those who believe and do good works, for them are the Gardens of Retreat - a welcome (in reward) for what they used to do

32:20.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فَسَقُواْ فَمَأۡوَىٰهُمُ ٱلنَّارُۖ كُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓاْ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَآ أُعِيدُواْ فِيهَا وَقِيلَ لَهُمۡ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ
32:20.en: And as for those who do evil, their retreat is the Fire. Whenever they desire to issue forth from thence, they are brought back thither. Unto them it is said: Taste the torment of the Fire which ye used to deny

32:21.ar: وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ دُونَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَكۡبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
32:21.en: And verily We make them taste the lower punishment before the greater, that haply they may return

32:22.ar: وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن ذُكِّرَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ ثُمَّ أَعۡرَضَ عَنۡهَآۚ إِنَّا مِنَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُنتَقِمُونَ
32:22.en: And who doth greater wrong than he who is reminded of the revelations of his Lord, then turneth from them. Lo! We shall requite the guilty

32:23.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ فَلَا تَكُن فِي مِرۡيَةࣲ مِّن لِّقَآئِهِۦۖ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ هُدࣰ ى لِّبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ
32:23.en: We verily gave Moses the Scripture; so be not ye in doubt of his receiving it; and We appointed it a guidance for the Children of Israel

32:24.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡ أَئِمَّةࣰ يَهۡدُونَ بِأَمۡرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُواْۖ وَكَانُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يُوقِنُونَ
32:24.en: And when they became steadfast and believed firmly in Our revelations, We appointed from among them leaders who guided by Our command

32:25.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ يَفۡصِلُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ فِيمَا كَانُواْ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَ
32:25.en: Lo! thy Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ

17:58.ar: وَإِن مِّن قَرۡيَةٍ إِلَّا نَحۡنُ مُهۡلِكُوهَا قَبۡلَ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ أَوۡ مُعَذِّبُوهَا عَذَابࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ اۚ كَانَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مَسۡطُورࣰ ا
17:58.en: There is not a township but We shall destroy it ere the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with dire punishment. That is set forth in the Book (of Our decrees)

106:2.en: For their taming (We cause) the caravans to set forth in winter and summer

53:16.en: When that which shroudeth did enshroud the lote-tree

52:21.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱتَّبَعَتۡهُمۡ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم بِإِيمَٰنٍ أَلۡحَقۡنَا بِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَمَآ أَلَتۡنَٰهُم مِّنۡ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَيۡءࣲۚ كُلُّ ٱمۡرِيِٕۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينࣱ‏
52:21.en: And they who believe and whose seed follow them in faith, We cause their seed to join them (there), and We deprive them of nought of their (life's) work. Every man is a pledge for that which he hath earned

6:158.ar: هَلۡ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن تَأۡتِيَهُمُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ أَوۡ يَأۡتِيَ رَبُّكَ أَوۡ يَأۡتِيَ بَعۡضُ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكَۗ يَوۡمَ يَأۡتِي بَعۡضُ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكَ لَا يَنفَعُ نَفۡسًا إِيمَٰنُهَا لَمۡ تَكُنۡ ءَامَنَتۡ مِن قَبۡلُ أَوۡ كَسَبَتۡ فِيٓ إِيمَٰنِهَا خَيۡرࣰ اۗ قُلِ ٱنتَظِرُوٓاْ إِنَّا مُنتَظِرُونَ
6:158.en: Wait they, indeed, for nothing less than that the angels should come unto them, or thy Lord should come, or there should come one of the portents from thy Lord? In the day when one of the portents from thy Lord cometh, its belief availeth naught a soul which theretofore believed not, nor in its belief earned good (by works). Say: Wait ye! Lo! We (too) are waiting

9e5FKgNqtEQ.speaker: adnan
9e5FKgNqtEQ.speaker_note: the sheikh's Sunday Arabic tafsir closing As-Sajdah; he mentions teaching fiqh and Tahawi's creed and his work as a physician
9e5FKgNqtEQ.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat As-Sajdah (verses 26-30, conclusion)
9e5FKgNqtEQ.one_line: Religious leaders are followed for their state with Allah; reflecting on obvious blessings like rain on dead land, gratitude, and the Day of Opening.
9e5FKgNqtEQ.summary: He opens by arguing that in religion, unlike medicine or car repair, a scholar is followed for his state with Allah, not only his intelligence; brilliant thinkers without piety were forgotten, while Abu Hanifa, Tahawi and Nawawi endured. If the Quran has not changed Muslims, he finds it hard to present it to others. In verse 26 he distinguishes kinds of guidance: some truths, like the fate of past nations whose ruins we walk through, are reachable by reflection alone, while others, such as Allah's mercy or the harm of alcohol, need revelation, which medicine confirmed only after enormous damage. Verse 27 asks us to notice the obvious: water on dead land brings crops for us and our livestock, something no one could fix if it stopped. Taking such blessings for granted, like a child who treats his allowance as owed, destroys gratitude, and a relationship with Allah conditional on a certain level of comfort cannot last. The scoffers' question about 'the Opening' uses a word unique to this surah: for the believer the Day is an opening into delights we lack the senses to grasp, while faith then no longer helps. The Prophet is told to turn away and wait, and believers should avoid company that weakens their bond with Allah.

outline.heading: Every command and prohibition aims at nearness
outline.gist: The whole deen simplifies to one idea: what brings you closer to Allah until your side cannot rest in bed.

outline.heading: In religion a scholar is followed for his state
outline.gist: We do not ask a doctor or mechanic about his piety, but a religious guide must have a state with Allah; many brilliant thinkers were forgotten for lacking it.

outline.heading: The Prophet's state was more eloquent than his words
outline.gist: Abu Hanifa was followed because he prayed at night and was scrupulous; the Prophet's conduct moved hearts even more than his speech.

outline.heading: Why he lingers on scholars' biographies
outline.gist: He spends fiqh lessons on the lives of authors; Tahawi's creed survived a thousand years because of its author's piety, acknowledged even by critics.

outline.heading: Nawawi and al-Subki's reverence
outline.gist: Nawawi died around forty, unmarried, yet his works endure; Taqi al-Din al-Subki rubbed his face on the floor Nawawi had walked on.

outline.heading: Knowledge that did not benefit you cannot benefit me
outline.gist: If your learning gave you no relationship with Allah, what can others hope from it?

outline.heading: Ashamed to offer what has not changed us
outline.gist: If Muslim societies have not benefited from the Quran, a non-Muslim can fairly ask why its beauty is not visible in us.

outline.heading: Recap of the surah's central verses
outline.gist: Gratitude, nearness, hidden delight, believer and sinner unequal, the lesser punishment, and Musa.

outline.heading: Recitation of the closing verses
outline.gist: He reads the verses on destroyed nations and rain on barren land.

outline.heading: Kinds of guidance, and what you can reach yourself
outline.gist: Some guidance comes by reflection; as with a child, you should not be handed what you can work out alone, while Allah's mercy, forgiveness and love need revelation.

outline.heading: Revelation spares the harm of trial and error
outline.gist: People may see no harm in consensual zina; medicine now says no amount of alcohol is safe, but only after millions of lives and billions of dollars were lost.

outline.heading: Walking through the dwellings of destroyed nations
outline.gist: No revelation is needed to see that generation after generation of tyrants perished; every land has the same story.

outline.heading: Ruins as signs: will they not hear?
outline.gist: Those who called revelation ancient myths and grew self-sufficient vanished, leaving palaces that tourists now visit.

outline.heading: Water driven to barren land
outline.gist: Dead land revives; livestock are mentioned first because we eat both the crops and the animals that eat them.

outline.heading: Reflect on the obvious
outline.gist: The Quran asks us to stop at what we take for granted: if seeds did not sprout after watering, whom would you complain to?

outline.heading: Every nation perishes, and so will you
outline.gist: These shared truths, death and rain, unite all humans and should send them back to Allah.

outline.heading: Blessings taken for granted
outline.gist: A child who treats his allowance as owed and stops respecting you mirrors how we treat Allah's gifts; Quraysh's familiarity with their trade journeys is the same disease, and it causes blessings to vanish.

outline.heading: Without gratitude the relationship dies
outline.gist: Little do you thank opened the surah's account of us; love cannot grow without constant gratitude, even for the basics alone.

outline.heading: A relationship conditional on comfort
outline.gist: If you love Him only while He keeps your standard of living, it is not a sound relationship; health, children and wealth are pure extras.

outline.heading: 'When is this Opening?' and a common recitation mistake
outline.gist: Their faith is the subject of the verb, so 'imanuhum' ends in damma: on that day their faith will not benefit the disbelievers.

outline.heading: Why 'the Opening' only here
outline.gist: Nowhere else is the Day called the Opening; the scoffer echoes the believer's description of meeting Allah as an opening into His gardens.

outline.heading: We lack the tools to know what is hidden
outline.gist: The Prophet could only describe what he saw as light; a small child cannot grasp adult intimacy and a man born blind cannot grasp colour.

outline.heading: The preacher's description and the scoffer's mockery
outline.gist: Preachers try to wake hearts by describing the Day, and the one who turns away asks sarcastically when it will be.

outline.heading: The Day as an opening for the lover of Allah
outline.gist: The book in the right hand, the Prophet's pool, reunion with family and entering paradise behind the Prophet.

outline.heading: Faith that comes too late
outline.gist: On that day everyone believes and is humbled, but faith not earned earlier does not benefit and no respite is given.

outline.heading: An atom of faith now counts
outline.gist: In this life a little more faith raises you and Allah answers a span with an arm's length.

outline.heading: Turn away and wait
outline.gist: Waiting in the Quran always refers to punishment; they chose to live awaiting it.

outline.heading: Protect your bond from company that corrupts it
outline.gist: We are not judges over people; we offer what we found, treat colleagues of no faith kindly, but avoid companionship, even with Muslims, that pulls us from Allah.

outline.heading: Starting each week with this surah
outline.gist: Friday, the best day, opens the Muslim week, and As-Sajdah in its Fajr makes the first priority returning to Allah.

outline.heading: Outro

27:82.ar: ۞وَإِذَا وَقَعَ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَخۡرَجۡنَا لَهُمۡ دَآبَّةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمۡ أَنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ كَانُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا لَا يُوقِنُونَ
27:82.en: And when the word is fulfilled concerning them, We shall bring forth a beast of the earth to speak unto them because mankind had not faith in Our revelations

27:83.ar: وَيَوۡمَ نَحۡشُرُ مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةࣲ فَوۡجࣰ ا مِّمَّن يُكَذِّبُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَهُمۡ يُوزَعُونَ
27:83.en: And (remind them of) the Day when We shall gather out of every nation a host of those who denied Our revelations, and they will be set in array

27:84.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُو قَالَ أَكَذَّبۡتُم بِـَٔايَٰتِي وَلَمۡ تُحِيطُواْ بِهَا عِلۡمًا أَمَّاذَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
27:84.en: Till, when they come (before their Lord), He will say: Did ye deny My revelations when ye could not compass them in knowledge, or what was it that ye did

27:85.ar: وَوَقَعَ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَيۡهِم بِمَا ظَلَمُواْ فَهُمۡ لَا يَنطِقُونَ
27:85.en: And the Word will be fulfilled concerning them because they have done wrong, and they will not speak

27:86.ar: أَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلَّيۡلَ لِيَسۡكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَٱلنَّهَارَ مُبۡصِرًاۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
27:86.en: Have they not seen how We have appointed the night that they may rest therein, and the day sight-giving? Lo! therein verily are portents for a people who believe

27:87.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَكُلٌّ أَتَوۡهُ دَٰخِرِينَ
27:87.en: And (remind them of) the Day when the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will start in fear, save him whom Allah willeth. And all come unto Him, humbled

27:88.ar: وَتَرَى ٱلۡجِبَالَ تَحۡسَبُهَا جَامِدَةࣰ وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ ٱلسَّحَابِۚ صُنۡعَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَتۡقَنَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍۚ إِنَّهُۥ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
27:88.en: And thou seest the hills thou deemest solid flying with the flight of clouds: the doing of Allah Who perfecteth all things. Lo! He is Informed of what ye do

27:89.ar: مَن جَآءَ بِٱلۡحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَهُم مِّن فَزَعࣲ يَوۡمَئِذٍ ءَامِنُونَ
27:89.en: Whoso bringeth a good deed will have better than its worth; and such are safe from fear that Day

27:90.ar: وَمَن جَآءَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ فَكُبَّتۡ وُجُوهُهُمۡ فِي ٱلنَّارِ هَلۡ تُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
27:90.en: And whoso bringeth an ill-deed, such will be flung down on their faces in the Fire. Are ye rewarded aught save what ye did

27:91.ar: إِنَّمَآ أُمِرۡتُ أَنۡ أَعۡبُدَ رَبَّ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡبَلۡدَةِ ٱلَّذِي حَرَّمَهَا وَلَهُۥ كُلُّ شَيۡءࣲۖ وَأُمِرۡتُ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
27:91.en: (Say): I (Muhammad) am commanded only to serve the Lord of this land which He hath hallowed, and unto Whom all things belong. And I am commanded to be of those who surrender (unto Him)

27:92.ar: وَأَنۡ أَتۡلُوَاْ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَۖ فَمَنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهۡتَدِي لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَقُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنذِرِينَ
27:92.en: And to recite the Qur'an. And whoso goeth right, goeth right only for (the good of) his own soul; and as for him who goeth astray - (Unto him) say: Lo! I am only a warner

49:17.ar: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيۡكَ أَنۡ أَسۡلَمُواْۖ قُل لَّا تَمُنُّواْ عَلَيَّ إِسۡلَٰمَكُمۖ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنۡ هَدَىٰكُمۡ لِلۡإِيمَٰنِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
49:17.en: They make it a favour unto thee (Muhammad) that they have surrendered (unto Him). Say: Deem not your Surrender a favour unto me; but Allah doth confer a favour on you, inasmuch as He hath led you to the Faith, if ye are earnest

27:93.ar: وَقُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ فَتَعۡرِفُونَهَاۚ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
27:93.en: And say: Praise be to Allah Who will show you His portents so that ye shall know them. And thy Lord is not unaware of what ye (mortals) do

tcP_N_YdfWQ.speaker: adnan
tcP_N_YdfWQ.speaker_note: Continues his own 'Listening to the Divine' series in his bilingual khutbah format.
tcP_N_YdfWQ.title: Listening to the Divine: An-Naml 82-93
tcP_N_YdfWQ.one_line: The end of An-Naml: on Judgment Day the deniers are asked 'what were you doing?'; reflect on the signs, seek guidance for yourself.
tcP_N_YdfWQ.summary: The final khutbah of his run through Surat An-Naml (27:82-93). He places the surah at the end of a Quranic axis running from Al-Isra about carrying the message, where An-Naml adds that strength, civilization and knowledge are the tools that let the bearer of the message be heard, which is why Sulayman could bring a whole kingdom to Islam while prophets without power were ignored. The closing verses jump to the Last Day: the creature from the earth, the gathering of those who denied, and the question he says he still fears for himself: did you deny My signs without ever studying them, or what were you doing? The deniers fall silent because their life's book has no plot. Allah then points to the most obvious sign, night for rest and day for sight, which needs no scientist to grasp, and to mountains that move like clouds. Good deeds bring better and safety from the terror of that Day. From 27:92 he draws his main application: guidance benefits only the one guided, so stop expecting applause for being good, as the Bedouins did in 49:17, and do good as selfishly as you can for your own salvation. He closes by asking the congregation not to grow oblivious to Gaza, Sudan and Yemen.

outline.heading: Opening
Recitation of 27:82-86
outline.gist: He recites the passage from the creature brought out of the earth to night made for rest and day for sight.

outline.heading: Interlude
The last surah of an axis: strength makes the message heard
outline.gist: The surahs from Al-Isra onward deal with carrying the message, what it requires and what holds it back. An-Naml adds the impact of strength, civilization and knowledge: Musa, Salih and Lut lacked power and were not heeded, while Sulayman brought a whole kingdom to Islam.

outline.heading: The creature from the earth
outline.gist: When the word befalls them, the earth that produced all of us produces one last creature that tells the truth: people did not have certainty in Allah's signs.

outline.heading: The deniers gathered from every nation
outline.gist: A group from every nation that denied the signs is driven together and asked: did you deny My signs without encompassing them in knowledge?

outline.heading: Or what were you doing?
outline.gist: Did you spend any time seeking to understand them? If not, what were you doing for seventy-five years: what did you look at, what did you learn, what conclusions did you draw?

outline.heading: The word falls and they cannot speak
outline.gist: The sentence falls on them for their wrongdoing and they are struck silent; then the verse asks whether they did not see that night was made for rest and day for sight.

outline.heading: Reflect on the obvious: night and day
outline.gist: The Quran keeps asking us to reflect on what every functioning human shares, needing no scientist, scholar or wealth: the cycle of night and day without which we could not survive or become what we are.

outline.heading: The trumpet blast
outline.gist: On the Day the trumpet is blown, all in the heavens and the earth are terrified except whom Allah wills, and all come to Him humbled.

outline.heading: Mountains that pass like clouds
outline.gist: You think the mountains are fixed but they pass like clouds, whose slow movement you cannot detect without tools; the work of Allah who perfected everything.

outline.heading: Good brings better; evil, face first
outline.gist: Whoever comes with a good deed receives better and is safe from the terror of that Day; whoever comes with evil is thrown face first into the Fire. Are you repaid for anything but what you did?

outline.heading: The Prophet's commission
outline.gist: He was commanded only to worship the Lord of this city which He made sacred, to be among the Muslims and to recite the Quran; whoever is guided is guided for himself.

outline.heading: Guidance is for yourself
outline.gist: No one else benefits from your guidance. Do not seek it for the collective, for the ummah to improve or for your parents to be happy; seek it because you need it.

outline.heading: No one owes you applause
outline.gist: Being good can leave you feeling owed. Some Bedouins acted as though their Islam was a favour to the Prophet (49:17); if you are guided, you are the one who carries the debt.

outline.heading: Do good as selfishly as possible
outline.gist: He does this to save himself and cannot hide in a cave after all he was given. Look at what Allah gave you, work out what you must do with it, and do it not out of altruism but so you are well on that Day.

outline.heading: He will show you His signs
outline.gist: Whoever strays, say I am only a warner; say praise be to Allah, He will show you His signs and you will recognize them.

outline.heading: Interlude
Closing a long Quranic axis
outline.gist: In Arabic: An-Naml ends the axis that begins at Al-Isra on carrying the message, presenting strength, civilization and knowledge as the tools by which its bearer fulfils the trust, and closes with the final moments of existence.

outline.heading: Turning away from signs in front of you
outline.gist: The case of a lifetime is denying signs that are plain in front of you and never investing time or effort to understand them. He still hears the question 'what were you doing?' and fears it for himself.

outline.heading: Your book has no beginning or end
outline.gist: He imagines being told: explain what you did; your book is muddled, its reader can find no thread in it. They sit silent, unable to answer.

outline.heading: The sign that turns an atheist into a believer
outline.gist: The verse that can shake a person from disbelief to faith is simply night for rest and day for sight; without it you would not exist.

outline.heading: Whoever searches for His signs will see them
outline.gist: The Prophet's only charge was to worship, submit and recite; whoever seeks guidance finds it for himself and whoever strays bears it. Allah shows His signs to everyone who searches, so do not turn from them or face a question that silences the tongue.

outline.heading: What is the plot?
outline.gist: In English: you will be asked something you cannot answer. Looking at your book: where is the story, what is the plot, what did you spend this time doing?

outline.heading: Apple made this phone
outline.gist: The sun, the moon, the mountains and the rivers were all there and none was worth a moment's thought or a conclusion. What was more interesting? The phone, and the reels were endless.

outline.heading: Guidance is sought for oneself: the surah's last word
outline.gist: The Prophet was told only to worship the Lord of the sacred city, submit to Him and follow the Quran; those who seek guidance seek it for themselves and the rest bear the consequences.

outline.heading: Interlude
Do not be oblivious to Gaza, Sudan and Yemen
outline.gist: Months after the fighting paused, people in Gaza are still dying, freezing and hungry; Sudan is one of the worst humanitarian crises in decades, and Yemen suffers too. Keep advocating, making dua and attending to their needs.

outline.heading: Outro

2:96.en: And thou wilt find them greediest of mankind for life and (greedier) than the idolaters. (Each) one of them would like to be allowed to live a thousand years. And to live (a thousand years) would be no means remove him from the doom. Allah is Seer of what they do

2:28.ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمۡ أَمۡوَٰتࣰ ا فَأَحۡيَٰكُمۡۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ

7jNej9QLESE.title: Tazkiyah Halaqa: Mortality, Episode 28
7jNej9QLESE.one_line: Accepting mortality is not inviting death: it frees you to live joyfully, tames the nafs, and cures the ummah's weakness (wahn).
7jNej9QLESE.summary: He opens with a disclaimer: Islam treats life as precious, forbids harming the body, obliges seeking treatment and teaches not to wish for battle. Accepting mortality is meant to beautify life, not cheapen it. Using the Prophet's life of eighteen close bereavements, exile and betrayal, he shows that someone at peace with mortality can stay upbeat, while any unresolved reality, like an unstudied exam or buried trauma, paralyses us and turns joy into distraction. Death is the heaviest such reality and lies in the future; denial shows in the midlife crisis. Since the nafs, unlike the spirit, fears death above all, mortality is the weapon that tames it, and it lets sermons about death motivate rather than cripple. He gives practical steps: name your fears, such as leaving children behind, which he illustrates with his grandfather's dying plea that his children keep their deen; write and regularly renew a will; and examine what you fear missing out on. He closes with the hadith of nations devouring the ummah because of wahn, love of this world and hatred of death, linking it to colonialism and dictatorship, and explains that fearing death more than losing your principles means you stand for nothing. The fear of not having done enough is healthy when balanced by knowing Allah does not want to punish.

outline.heading: Allah's accountability versus self-accountability
outline.gist: Accepting mortality is incomplete without accepting that Allah will hold us accountable, which differs from holding ourselves to account.

outline.heading: Not an invitation to death
outline.gist: Life is precious; death is something to avoid, though not at the cost of values, principles and dignity.

outline.heading: The health of the body comes before perfect form in worship
outline.gist: Someone with bad knees or back must pray on a chair; harming the body to pray correctly is sinful.

outline.heading: Smoking, drugs and seeking treatment
outline.gist: What is only harmful is forbidden, treatment is obligatory, and the Prophet told companions not to wish to meet the enemy.

outline.heading: Accepting the inevitable beautifies life
outline.gist: Making peace with mortality makes every moment more precious rather than cheapening life.

outline.heading: Sort it out or live under a dark cloud
outline.gist: Unresolved, death lingers and ruins your mood whenever loss or a bad diagnosis comes.

outline.heading: The Prophet's losses
outline.gist: Orphaned young and denied an education, he lost Khadijah, his sons, three daughters, uncles, aunts and cousins, around eighteen close deaths, yet remained upbeat.

outline.heading: Exiled and betrayed, yet joyful
outline.gist: He never returned to live in Mecca, was betrayed repeatedly and worn down, yet stayed kind and joking because he had dealt with mortality.

outline.heading: An unresolved reality paralyses you
outline.gist: Like an exam you are not studying for, an unaddressed reality blocks every other part of life.

outline.heading: Joy as distraction is not joy
outline.gist: Good times used to forget a looming problem are not real until the problem is dealt with.

outline.heading: Death is the heaviest reality
outline.gist: Nothing compares to it; distraction enlarges the void, and people fall into addictions trying to forget.

outline.heading: Dealing with buried pain
outline.gist: Therapy requires facing what you avoid; men bottle up old embarrassments and betrayals and must accept them to move on.

outline.heading: Mortality is trauma from the future
outline.gist: Past hurts can be accepted and made peace with, but death lies ahead, which is why accepting it is a priority in Islam.

outline.heading: The midlife crisis as denial
outline.gist: Men in their forties dye their hair and act young when reminded they are past the peak; he jokes about the reminders since turning 40, though the spirit does not age.

outline.heading: Age is relative; work out for the right reason
outline.gist: Old is only old in comparison; exercise to preserve the body Allah gave, not to run from what you are running towards.

outline.heading: What the spirit and the nafs fear
outline.gist: Both fear pain, but only the nafs, born of body and spirit together, fears death, which makes mortality the ultimate weapon against it.

outline.heading: Why he teaches this piece midway
outline.gist: People must first try to strive against the nafs and see how hard it is; the Prophet said remembering death is enough.

outline.heading: Why sermons about death fail
outline.gist: He cannot give emotive reminders in most communities because listeners' hopes are still worldly and their fear of death cripples them; once at peace, such reminders motivate.

outline.heading: Quranic reminders all tie back to mortality
outline.gist: The companions were moved by recitation alone; after intellectual conviction, ongoing motivation is needed against desensitisation.

outline.heading: Love, and desires aligned with revelation
outline.gist: Love is the best motive but takes time; full faith is when desires follow what the Prophet brought, and the nafs can adapt to anything except death.

outline.heading: Accept mortality first so it frightens only the nafs
outline.gist: If you fear death too, reminders make you anxious and avoidant; accepted, they strengthen you.

outline.heading: Fear one: those you leave behind
outline.gist: Parents fear how orphans are treated; admit it, plan with your spouse and make dua for your children.

outline.heading: His grandfather's dying plea
outline.gist: His grandfather died at 39 with ten children and kept begging a friend to make sure his children kept their deen; that friend later taught him.

outline.heading: Write and renew your will
outline.gist: Write what you want loved ones to know and how your legacy should continue, renew it every few months, and arrange provision for dependants.

outline.heading: Fear two: missing out
outline.gist: Do halal things you would regret missing; regretting a sin you never committed is worse than the sin; you do not truly miss events since existence continues.

outline.heading: Death ends your ability to change outcomes
outline.gist: This phase decides the others; later realisations will mean nothing, while changes now mean a lot.

outline.heading: The hadith of nations devouring the ummah
outline.gist: Nations will call one another to devour you like a dish, not because you are few but because you are like foam on the sea.

outline.heading: Wahn: love of this world and hatred of death
outline.gist: The Prophet gave wahn a specific meaning; excessive fear of death makes people avoid it at any cost and so stand for nothing.

outline.heading: Fear of death versus fear of losing principles
outline.gist: If a gun to your head ends your stand for justice, you never stood for it; those who cling to any life regardless of dignity are described in the Quran.

outline.heading: Life is the first blessing
outline.gist: Muslims cherish life as Allah's greatest gift, before even guidance, yet do not sell out principles to keep it.

outline.heading: The prophecy fulfilled: colonialism and dictators
outline.gist: Sykes-Picot, colonisation, stolen resources, lost language and deen, then decades of dictators fulfilled the hadith.

outline.heading: The cause still stands today
outline.gist: Fear of death still dictates what Muslims say and choose; the Prophet taught us to use mortality to tame the nafs instead.

outline.heading: Death will find us standing
outline.gist: We neither hasten nor celebrate death, but will not run or change who we are when it comes; hence 'pray as if it is your last prayer'.

outline.heading: Why 'your last prayer' works
outline.gist: Reminded it may die, the nafs is scared quiet, and the prayer becomes focused and enjoyable.

outline.heading: Fear three: not having done enough
outline.gist: This natural fear is designed to motivate, not paralyse, pushing you forward to avoid pain.

outline.heading: Allah does not want to punish you
outline.gist: What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? Distorted views of God either paralyse or switch fear off; the truthful balance moves you forward.

outline.heading: Outro

11:36.ar: وَأُوحِيَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُۥ لَن يُؤۡمِنَ مِن قَوۡمِكَ إِلَّا مَن قَدۡ ءَامَنَ فَلَا تَبۡتَئِسۡ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
11:36.en: And it was inspired in Noah, (saying): No-one of thy folk will believe save him who hath believed already. Be not distressed because of what they do

11:37.ar: وَٱصۡنَعِ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَا وَوَحۡيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبۡنِي فِي ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِنَّهُم مُّغۡرَقُونَ
11:37.en: Build the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and speak not unto Me on behalf of those who do wrong. Lo! they will be drowned

11:38.ar: وَيَصۡنَعُ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيۡهِ مَلَأࣱ مِّن قَوۡمِهِۦ سَخِرُواْ مِنۡهُۚ قَالَ إِن تَسۡخَرُواْ مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسۡخَرُ مِنكُمۡ كَمَا تَسۡخَرُونَ
11:38.en: And he was building the ship, and every time that chieftains of his people passed him, they made mock of him. He said: Though ye make mock of Us, yet We mock at you even as ye mock

11:39.ar: فَسَوۡفَ تَعۡلَمُونَ مَن يَأۡتِيهِ عَذَابࣱ يُخۡزِيهِ وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيۡهِ عَذَابࣱ مُّقِيمٌ
11:39.en: And ye shall know to whom a punishment that will confound him cometh, and upon whom a lasting doom will fall

11:40.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمۡرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلۡنَا ٱحۡمِلۡ فِيهَا مِن كُلࣲّ زَوۡجَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ وَأَهۡلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ وَمَنۡ ءَامَنَۚ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱ‏
11:40.en: (Thus it was) till, when Our commandment came to pass and the oven gushed forth water, We said: Load therein two of every kind, a pair (the male and female), and thy household, save him against whom the word hath gone forth already, and those who believe. And but a few were they who believed with him

11:41.ar: ۞وَقَالَ ٱرۡكَبُواْ فِيهَا بِسۡمِ ٱللَّهِ مَجۡرٜىٰهَا وَمُرۡسَىٰهَآۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَغَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
11:41.en: And he said: Embark therein! In the name of Allah be its course and its mooring. Lo! my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful

11:42.ar: وَهِيَ تَجۡرِي بِهِمۡ فِي مَوۡجࣲ كَٱلۡجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبۡنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِي مَعۡزِلࣲ يَٰبُنَيَّ ٱرۡكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
11:42.en: And it sailed with them amid waves like mountains, and Noah cried unto his son - and he was standing aloof - O my son! Come ride with us, and be not with the disbelievers

11:43.ar: قَالَ سَـَٔاوِيٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلࣲ يَعۡصِمُنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِۚ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَۚ وَحَالَ بَيۡنَهُمَا ٱلۡمَوۡجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُغۡرَقِينَ
11:43.en: He said: I shall betake me to some mountain that will save me from the water. (Noah) said: This day there is none that saveth from the commandment of Allah save him on whom He hath had mercy. And the wave came in between them, so he was among the drowned

11:44.ar: وَقِيلَ يَٰٓأَرۡضُ ٱبۡلَعِي مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقۡلِعِي وَغِيضَ ٱلۡمَآءُ وَقُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ وَٱسۡتَوَتۡ عَلَى ٱلۡجُودِيِّۖ وَقِيلَ بُعۡدࣰ ا لِّلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
11:44.en: And it was said: O earth! Swallow thy water and, O sky! be cleared of clouds! And the water was made to subside. And the commandment was fulfilled. And it (the ship) came to rest upon (the mount) Al-Judi and it was said: A far removal for wrongdoing folk

11:45.ar: وَنَادَىٰ نُوحࣱ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبۡنِي مِنۡ أَهۡلِي وَإِنَّ وَعۡدَكَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحۡكَمُ ٱلۡحَٰكِمِينَ
11:45.en: And Noah cried unto his Lord and said: My Lord! Lo! my son is of my household! Surely Thy promise is the truth and Thou are the Most Just of Judges

11:46.ar: قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيۡسَ مِنۡ أَهۡلِكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيۡرُ صَٰلِحࣲۖ فَلَا تَسۡـَٔلۡنِ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۖ إِنِّيٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
11:46.en: He said: O Noah! Lo! he is not of thy household; lo! he is of evil conduct, so ask not of Me that whereof thou hast no knowledge. I admonish thee lest thou be among the ignorant

11:47.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّيٓ أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنۡ أَسۡـَٔلَكَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱۖ وَإِلَّا تَغۡفِرۡ لِي وَتَرۡحَمۡنِيٓ أَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
11:47.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! in Thee do I seek refuge (from the sin) that I should ask of Thee that whereof I have no knowledge. Unless Thou forgive me and have mercy on me I shall be among the lost

9:25.ar: لَقَدۡ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةࣲ وَيَوۡمَ حُنَيۡنٍ إِذۡ أَعۡجَبَتۡكُمۡ كَثۡرَتُكُمۡ فَلَمۡ تُغۡنِ عَنكُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتۡ ثُمَّ وَلَّيۡتُم مُّدۡبِرِينَ
9:25.en: Allah hath given you victory on many fields and on the day of Huneyn, when ye exulted in your multitude but it availed you naught, and the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for you; then ye turned back in flight

y29qPdsdq1I.speaker: adnan
y29qPdsdq1I.speaker_note: Continues his own 'Listening to the Divine' series in his bilingual khutbah format.
y29qPdsdq1I.title: Listening to the Divine: Hud 36-49
y29qPdsdq1I.one_line: Nuh and his drowned son: get on board, parents do their best without judging others, weak communities lose their youth, no lineage saves anyone.
y29qPdsdq1I.summary: A short khutbah in his Listening to the Divine series on Hud 36-49, the story of Nuh and the flood, framed by the reminder that Allah spoke to us long before we spoke to Him, so we listen before we formulate what we want to say. He walks through the verses: the heartrending revelation that no one else would believe, which Nuh accepted yet could not stop pleading against; the mockery of the prophet turned carpenter; the loading of the ark; and the call to a son who was in ma'zil, isolated both in the water and in how he had lived. The son trusts a mountain, the wave comes between them, and the earth swallows its water. He calls it one of the hardest stories in the Quran: a man who spent centuries guiding others could not reach his own child. The lessons are that get on board is figurative as well as literal, that this can happen in any family so parents must give everything and never judge others whose children stray, and that weak communities which fail to give youth an identity lose them to isolation while our numbers lull us. Finally, he is not of your family: no lineage saves anyone, which sets the deen's anti-corruption principle.

outline.heading: Opening
Recitation of Hud 36-39
outline.gist: He recites the passage from the revelation that none of Nuh's people will believe beyond those who already have, through the mockery of the chiefs and the warning of a lasting punishment.

outline.heading: Interlude
Listening before speaking
outline.gist: The series is about listening to Allah, who spoke to us informally through life and formally through the Book long before we found our voice; we are responding in this conversation, not initiating it.

outline.heading: No one else will believe: heartrending news
outline.gist: Nuh is told that only those who had already believed would believe. He knew it was true, but a messenger's hope to guide his people is a love ignited by love of Allah, so he could not help himself.

outline.heading: Do not plead for the wrongdoers
outline.gist: Told to build the ark under Allah's eyes and not to address Him about those who did wrong, Nuh still calls out for his people to be forgiven and guided; they are to be drowned.

outline.heading: The prophet turned carpenter
outline.gist: Each passing group of chiefs mocks him for becoming a carpenter after being a prophet; he answers that they will learn who receives the disgracing, lasting punishment. He adds the report that childbirth stopped among his people for seventy years before the flood, so none who drowned were children.

outline.heading: The oven gushes: loading the ark
outline.gist: When the command came and the tannur, the pit where bread is baked, gushed forth, he loaded a pair of every species, his family except those already decreed against, and the few who believed.

outline.heading: In the name of Allah its sailing and anchoring
outline.gist: Nuh tells them to board, invoking Allah over the ship's course and its rest; if you want to follow the prophets, be like them in this.

outline.heading: The son in isolation
outline.gist: Amid waves like mountains Nuh calls a son who was in ma'zil. Scholars read it as his position in the water or as how he lived; the sheikh thinks both, since the verse did not need the word to continue.

outline.heading: The mountain and the wave
outline.gist: The son trusts a mountain to protect him from the water; Nuh answers that nothing protects today from Allah's command except His mercy, and the wave comes between them.

outline.heading: Earth, swallow your water
outline.gist: The earth is told to swallow its water and the sky to withhold, the matter is concluded, the ark settles on Al-Judi, and the wrongdoing people are sent away.

outline.heading: One of the hardest stories in the Quran
outline.gist: A man who worked all his life to guide others could not reach his own son, and in a moment of weakness and love called him one last time, knowing he would refuse.

outline.heading: Get on board
outline.gist: The call is figurative as much as literal: why choose to stand on the other side?

outline.heading: It can happen in any family
outline.gist: Do your best in educating, mentoring and being there for your children, and never judge parents whose son or daughter went astray; Nuh's case is no excuse not to raise your kids.

outline.heading: Interlude
Every parent is shaken by this story
outline.gist: In Arabic: Nuh, among the resolute messengers and the proverbial model of patience and striving, called his people for centuries and had Allah's promise to save his family, yet this son was not saved; the story is the Quran's example of a parent's deepest pain.

outline.heading: Lost not to war but to weak communities
outline.gist: Parents today lose children not to disease or war but to loss of faith in communities that do not nurture their youth or root their identity. Nuh was not at fault: without enough believers he could not build a community to hold his son, and isolated youth drift until they cannot find the way back.

outline.heading: Numbers will fool you
outline.gist: Two billion Muslims comfort us into neglecting the next generation's deen, values and identity. The Prophet warned that numbers would fool us, and the Quran shows it at Hunayn; do not be fooled.

outline.heading: He is not of your family
outline.gist: Nuh pleads that his son is of his family and Allah's promise is true; Allah answers that he is not, his conduct was unrighteous, and Nuh must not ask about what he does not know. Nuh seeks refuge and forgiveness.

outline.heading: No lineage saves: the deen's anti-corruption principle
outline.gist: Allah does not care whose son you are or what country you come from; nothing is stronger than being a mighty prophet's son and it did not help. That sets the anti-corruption understanding of our deen for our communities and the countries we live in.

outline.heading: Outro
