76:5.ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡأَبۡرَارَ يَشۡرَبُونَ مِن كَأۡسࣲ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُورًا
76:5.en: Lo! the righteous shall drink of a cup whereof the mixture is of Kafur

76:6.ar: عَيۡنࣰ ا يَشۡرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ ٱللَّهِ يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفۡجِيرࣰ ا
76:6.en: A spring wherefrom the slaves of Allah drink, making it gush forth abundantly

76:7.ar: يُوفُونَ بِٱلنَّذۡرِ وَيَخَافُونَ يَوۡمࣰ ا كَانَ شَرُّهُۥ مُسۡتَطِيرࣰ ا
76:7.en: (Because) they perform the vow and fear a day whereof the evil is wide-spreading

76:8.ar: وَيُطۡعِمُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ مِسۡكِينࣰ ا وَيَتِيمࣰ ا وَأَسِيرًا
76:8.en: And feed with food the needy wretch, the orphan and the prisoner, for love of Him

76:9.ar: إِنَّمَا نُطۡعِمُكُمۡ لِوَجۡهِ ٱللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمۡ جَزَآءࣰ وَلَا شُكُورًا
76:9.en: (Saying): We feed you, for the sake of Allah only. We wish for no reward nor thanks from you

76:10.ar: إِنَّا نَخَافُ مِن رَّبِّنَا يَوۡمًا عَبُوسࣰ ا قَمۡطَرِيرࣰ ا
76:10.en: Lo! we fear from our Lord a day of frowning and of fate

76:11.ar: فَوَقَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ شَرَّ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمِ وَلَقَّىٰهُمۡ نَضۡرَةࣰ وَسُرُورࣰ ا
76:11.en: Therefor Allah hath warded off from them the evil of that day, and hath made them find brightness and joy

76:12.ar: وَجَزَىٰهُم بِمَا صَبَرُواْ جَنَّةࣰ وَحَرِيرࣰ ا
76:12.en: And hath awarded them for all that they endured, a Garden and silk attire

76:13.ar: مُّتَّكِـِٔينَ فِيهَا عَلَى ٱلۡأَرَآئِكِۖ لَا يَرَوۡنَ فِيهَا شَمۡسࣰ ا وَلَا زَمۡهَرِيرࣰ ا
76:13.en: Reclining therein upon couches, they will find there neither (heat of) a sun nor bitter cold

76:14.ar: وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيۡهِمۡ ظِلَٰلُهَا وَذُلِّلَتۡ قُطُوفُهَا تَذۡلِيلࣰ ا
76:14.en: The shade thereof is close upon them and the clustered fruits thereof bow down

76:15.ar: وَيُطَافُ عَلَيۡهِم بِـَٔانِيَةࣲ مِّن فِضَّةࣲ وَأَكۡوَابࣲ كَانَتۡ قَوَارِيرَا۠
76:15.en: Goblets of silver are brought round for them, and beakers (as) of glass

76:16.ar: قَوَارِيرَاْ مِن فِضَّةࣲ قَدَّرُوهَا تَقۡدِيرࣰ ا
76:16.en: (Bright as) glass but (made) of silver, which they (themselves) have measured to the measure (of their deeds)

76:1.ar: هَلۡ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ حِينࣱ مِّنَ ٱلدَّهۡرِ لَمۡ يَكُن شَيۡـࣰٔ ا مَّذۡكُورًا
76:1.en: Hath there come upon man (ever) any period of time in which he was a thing unremembered

76:2.ar: إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن نُّطۡفَةٍ أَمۡشَاجࣲ نَّبۡتَلِيهِ فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ سَمِيعَۢا بَصِيرًا
76:2.en: Lo! We create man from a drop of thickened fluid to test him; so We make him hearing, knowing

76:3.ar: إِنَّا هَدَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِرࣰ ا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا
76:3.en: Lo! We have shown him the way, whether he be grateful or disbelieving

76:4.ar: إِنَّآ أَعۡتَدۡنَا لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ سَلَٰسِلَاْ وَأَغۡلَٰلࣰ ا وَسَعِيرًا
76:4.en: Lo! We have prepared for disbelievers manacles and carcans and a raging fire

47:15.ar: مَّثَلُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَۖ فِيهَآ أَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّن مَّآءٍ غَيۡرِ ءَاسِنࣲ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّن لَّبَنࣲ لَّمۡ يَتَغَيَّرۡ طَعۡمُهُۥ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّنۡ خَمۡرࣲ لَّذَّةࣲ لِّلشَّٰرِبِينَ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّنۡ عَسَلࣲ مُّصَفࣰّ ىۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ وَمَغۡفِرَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ كَمَنۡ هُوَ خَٰلِدࣱ فِي ٱلنَّارِ وَسُقُواْ مَآءً حَمِيمࣰ ا فَقَطَّعَ أَمۡعَآءَهُمۡ
47:15.en: A similitude of the Garden which those who keep their duty (to Allah) are promised: Therein are rivers of water unpolluted, and rivers of milk whereof the flavour changeth not, and rivers of wine delicious to the drinkers, and rivers of clear-run honey; therein for them is every kind of fruit, with pardon from their Lord. (Are those who enjoy all this) like those who are immortal in the Fire and are given boiling water to drink so that it teareth their bowels

12:91.ar: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدۡ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِن كُنَّا لَخَٰطِـِٔينَ
12:91.en: They said: By Allah, verily Allah hath preferred thee above us, and we were indeed sinful

12:92.ar: قَالَ لَا تَثۡرِيبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ يَغۡفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
12:92.en: He said: Have no fear this day! May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy

aF7D-QCedmA.speaker: adnan
aF7D-QCedmA.speaker_note: regular tafseer voice; growing up in Syria and his teachers
aF7D-QCedmA.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Insan, Part 2: Verses 5-16
aF7D-QCedmA.one_line: Who the abrar are and what awaits them: keeping vows, feeding for Allah's face while wanting nothing back, and Paradise's complete, perfected bliss.
aF7D-QCedmA.summary: Continuing Al-Insan, he recalls the three modes of da'wah and notes that a caller must find each listener's key, while listeners should come wanting to be challenged rather than told what they like. Verses 5-6 describe the abrar, people of the highest virtue, drinking cups mixed with kafur from a spring they make gush at will. He asks listeners to notice how Paradise covers every category of bliss, physical, social, financial and spiritual, whose absence leaves an emptiness here. Verses 7-10 describe who they are: they keep their vows, a covenant like the shahadah itself, fear a day whose evil spreads, and feed the needy, orphan and captive out of love for Allah. He argues the surah is Makki: Ali and Fatimah giving away their meal was a family living a verse they already knew, just as the Prophet answered with Yusuf's words when his cousin repeated the brothers' apology. Feeding only for Allah's face means wanting no thanks, loyalty or vote in return, against the nafs, as Ali ibn al-Husayn did secretly for years. Verses 11-16 describe radiance, joy, silk, perfect weather, low fruit and flawless service. So why demand it now?

outline.heading: Al-Insan's dawah through desire
outline.gist: Al-Insan has the longest and richest description of Paradise because its dawah works through desire. Al-Qiyamah speaks to the mind first; desire for reward and fear of punishment are the two wings, and dawah needs all three.

outline.heading: Recap: count from the first blessing
outline.gist: The surah began before we existed so that we count every blessing from the very first, not from now; then gratitude grows and Paradise means more.

outline.heading: Reward never comes alone
outline.gist: Even this surah of Paradise has a verse of punishment; the Quran is never one-sided. The intellect is always addressed, as the first four verses did, and the balance depends on who you are speaking to.

outline.heading: Everyone has a key
outline.gist: His sheikh used to say each person has a key to their heart. A caller needs the wisdom to know what moves the person in front of him, or they will be bored even by the right message.

outline.heading: Not a request show: say what people need to hear
outline.gist: In a diverse community no speaker can please everyone. The listener has a share too: a speaker must be free to say what people need, challenging inherited stances and cultural baggage, not play requests like an old Arab call-in show.

outline.heading: Come wanting to be pushed
outline.gist: Come to the masjid wanting to change and be pushed forward. Feeling content with yourself is the worst state; always hold yourself to account.

outline.heading: The abrar: the highest level of virtue
outline.gist: After reciting, he explains al-abrar: from birr, the word used for treatment of parents, the highest level of ethics, ihsan made visible. They drink from a cup.

outline.heading: Cups from the rivers of Paradise
outline.gist: The Quran elsewhere describes rivers of pure water, wine that does not intoxicate, purified honey and milk, so the verse paints the virtuous seated with a cup.

outline.heading: Kafur: a costly delicacy, here a spring they make gush at will
outline.gist: Kafur was a rare, expensive Arabian spice with a refreshing scent. In Paradise it is a spring the servants of Allah use to flavour their drinks and can make burst from the ground wherever they wish.

outline.heading: Every category of bliss covered
outline.gist: Notice the categories of blessing: food and drink, physical, spiritual, psychological, social and financial. Missing any one leaves you unhappy; in Paradise every base is covered.

outline.heading: The emptiness that hits when people go home
outline.gist: People smile in company, then go home to their pain, their debts, their loneliness or their spiritual emptiness. It is a comfort that nothing will be missing there.

outline.heading: Who they are: they keep their vows
outline.gist: The verses turn briefly to describe the servants who enjoy this. The first trait is fulfilling vows.

outline.heading: Interlude
Vows must be kept; the shahadah is a covenant
outline.gist: A vow made to Allah must be kept; breaking it is expiated like a broken oath and is strongly disliked. Being good for your word includes the shahadah itself, a covenant to walk the Prophet's path.

outline.heading: A day whose evil flies beyond control
outline.gist: They truly fear a day whose evil is mustatir, from the root for flying: spreading beyond any containment.

outline.heading: Feeding the needy, orphan and captive for His love
outline.gist: He recites the next verses. 'Ala hubbihi can mean despite loving the food, but he prefers out of love for Allah: they feed the needy, the orphan and the prisoner for His love.

outline.heading: A sandwich for the love of Allah in Syria
outline.gist: In the Syria he grew up in, someone with no money could ask for food for the love of Allah or of the Prophet and be given a sandwich; those days had barakah.

outline.heading: Ali and Fatimah's meal
outline.gist: Some call the surah Madani because of these verses: Ali's household gave a third of their meal to a needy man, half to an orphan, and the rest to a captive, keeping nothing that night.

outline.heading: Living a verse already revealed
outline.gist: The order is the reverse: the surah was taught early, and the family seized the chance to practise it. The companions learned from the Prophet to look for situations the Quran describes and act as the good figure did.

outline.heading: Yusuf's words at the conquest
outline.gist: Coached by Ali, the Prophet's cousin Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, who had fought and reviled him for years, said what Yusuf's brothers said. Ali was certain the Prophet would answer as Yusuf did, and he did, without missing a beat.

outline.heading: Do it for His love
outline.gist: You want to be among these people, so do what they did: feed out of love for Allah, for all He has done for you, and nothing else.

outline.heading: Make your intentions big
outline.gist: Petty intentions leave you with petty results. Make big, sincere, ambitious intentions and the good and enjoyable things fall into place by themselves.

outline.heading: The teacher who fed orphans
outline.gist: One of his teachers cooked for an orphanage twice a week and was never happier than when watching the children eat. Food can be a joy you give, not only one you consume.

outline.heading: For the face of Allah: the highest level of Paradise
outline.gist: They feed only for the face of Allah, hoping to see Him. It is no coincidence that the word appears here: the highest people of Paradise see Allah morning and evening and care for nothing else.

outline.heading: We want nothing from you
outline.gist: Seeing His face is the only reason they give: they want no reward, no thanks, no gratitude. Take the food and go.

outline.heading: Not loyalty, favours or votes
outline.gist: Do not give and then wait for loyalty, support in a dispute or a vote when you run for office. You owe me nothing, not even a thank you: that is the heart of a Muslim.

outline.heading: The nafs wants some return
outline.gist: Giving for nothing takes conscious effort. The nafs accepts any petty return, a thank-you or public recognition, but cannot grasp giving with no return in this world.

outline.heading: Ali ibn al-Husayn's secret sacks of food
outline.gist: When Zayn al-Abidin was washed after death his back was scarred. A month later families came asking for their missing monthly food, and a merchant for his buyer: for years he had carried sacks to their doors at night, unknown even to his wife.

outline.heading: Give and walk away
outline.gist: Learn to give and walk away and you will live better. He never reminded anyone of a good he did, but always reminded people of the good they did him and repaid it again and again.

outline.heading: Flip the table on favours and harms
outline.gist: We fix on our favours to others and their harms to us; he saw their favours to him and worried about his harms to them. The Prophet and companions lived by what the Quran taught, which is why the verse was mistaken for a Madani one.

outline.heading: Fearing a frowning, dry day
outline.gist: They fear a day that is 'abus qamtarir: figuratively frowning and so dry that not one drop of good can be wrung from it, the same day whose evil spreads.

outline.heading: Radiance and joy in its place
outline.gist: Allah protected them from that day's evil and gave them nadrah, the freshness of one who is not parched, and joy; for their patience, a garden and silk.

outline.heading: Reclining, with neither scorching sun nor bitter cold
outline.gist: They recline on couches with their drinks on demand, seeing neither a blazing sun nor zamharir, extreme cold like today's.

outline.heading: Light from the land itself; perfect weather
outline.gist: Asked how there is light without a sun, the Prophet said the land of Paradise gives light. The weather is perfect, not London in winter.

outline.heading: Shade drawn close
outline.gist: The trees' shade hovers close and moves to wherever you want it.

outline.heading: Fruit humbled within reach
outline.gist: Dhullilat: the fruit is made humble and brought low, not out of reach like the apricots he and his friends were too lazy to climb for.

outline.heading: Served as you wish
outline.gist: Whatever you want comes to you and goes back when you are done: physical comfort and the psychological ease of being served, the reward for those who gave and wanted nothing back.

outline.heading: Silver-crystal cups measured to taste
outline.gist: After reciting two more verses: servants circulate with vessels of silver and cups of crystal made with silver, filled with exactly the amount you want.

outline.heading: Even the service is perfected
outline.gist: Some vessels are empty for you to fill as you ask, others already filled. Unlike a restaurant where hunger hides bad service, in Paradise the food and the service are both perfect.

outline.heading: Why demand it now? Prove yourself worthy
outline.gist: What more could you want? This world was never designed to hold these things, so stop asking for them now and prove yourself worthy of them.

76:13.en: Reclining therein upon couches, they will find there neither (heat of) a sun nor bitter cold

76:14.ar: وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيۡهِمۡ ظِلَٰلُهَا وَذُلِّلَتۡ قُطُوفُهَا تَذۡلِيلࣰ ا
76:14.en: The shade thereof is close upon them and the clustered fruits thereof bow down

76:15.ar: وَيُطَافُ عَلَيۡهِم بِـَٔانِيَةࣲ مِّن فِضَّةࣲ وَأَكۡوَابࣲ كَانَتۡ قَوَارِيرَا۠
76:15.en: Goblets of silver are brought round for them, and beakers (as) of glass

76:16.ar: قَوَارِيرَاْ مِن فِضَّةࣲ قَدَّرُوهَا تَقۡدِيرࣰ ا
76:16.en: (Bright as) glass but (made) of silver, which they (themselves) have measured to the measure (of their deeds)

76:17.ar: وَيُسۡقَوۡنَ فِيهَا كَأۡسࣰ ا كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلًا
76:17.en: There are they watered with a cup whereof the mixture is of Zanjabil

76:18.ar: عَيۡنࣰ ا فِيهَا تُسَمَّىٰ سَلۡسَبِيلࣰ ا
76:18.en: (The water of) a spring therein, named Salsabil

76:19.ar: ۞وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وِلۡدَٰنࣱ مُّخَلَّدُونَ إِذَا رَأَيۡتَهُمۡ حَسِبۡتَهُمۡ لُؤۡلُؤࣰ ا مَّنثُورࣰ ا
76:19.en: There wait on them immortal youths, whom, when thou seest, thou wouldst take for scattered pearls

76:20.ar: وَإِذَا رَأَيۡتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيۡتَ نَعِيمࣰ ا وَمُلۡكࣰ ا كَبِيرًا
76:20.en: When thou seest, thou wilt see there bliss and high estate

76:21.ar: عَٰلِيَهُمۡ ثِيَابُ سُندُسٍ خُضۡرࣱ وَإِسۡتَبۡرَقࣱۖ وَحُلُّوٓاْ أَسَاوِرَ مِن فِضَّةࣲ وَسَقَىٰهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ شَرَابࣰ ا طَهُورًا
76:21.en: Their raiment will be fine green silk and gold embroidery. Bracelets of silver will they wear. Their Lord will slake their thirst with a pure drink

76:22.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا كَانَ لَكُمۡ جَزَآءࣰ وَكَانَ سَعۡيُكُم مَّشۡكُورًا
76:22.en: (And it will be said unto them): Lo! this is a reward for you. Your endeavour (upon earth) hath found acceptance

76:23.ar: إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ تَنزِيلࣰ ا
76:23.en: Lo! We, even We, have revealed unto thee the Qur'an, a revelation

76:24.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تُطِعۡ مِنۡهُمۡ ءَاثِمًا أَوۡ كَفُورࣰ ا
76:24.en: So submit patiently to thy Lord's command, and obey not of them any guilty one or disbeliever

76:25.ar: وَٱذۡكُرِ ٱسۡمَ رَبِّكَ بُكۡرَةࣰ وَأَصِيلࣰ ا
76:25.en: Remember the name of thy Lord at morn and evening

76:26.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَٱسۡجُدۡ لَهُۥ وَسَبِّحۡهُ لَيۡلࣰ ا طَوِيلًا
76:26.en: And worship Him (a portion) of the night. And glorify Him through the livelong night

76:27.ar: إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يُحِبُّونَ ٱلۡعَاجِلَةَ وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَآءَهُمۡ يَوۡمࣰ ا ثَقِيلࣰ ا
76:27.en: Lo! these love fleeting life, and put behind them (the remembrance of) a grievous day

76:28.ar: نَّحۡنُ خَلَقۡنَٰهُمۡ وَشَدَدۡنَآ أَسۡرَهُمۡۖ وَإِذَا شِئۡنَا بَدَّلۡنَآ أَمۡثَٰلَهُمۡ تَبۡدِيلًا
76:28.en: We, even We, created them, and strengthened their frame. And when We will, We can replace them, bringing others like them in their stead

76:29.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦ تَذۡكِرَةࣱۖ فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ سَبِيلࣰ ا

76:30.en: Yet ye will not, unless Allah willeth. Lo! Allah is Knower, Wise

95DMR6oenpU.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Insan, Part 3: Verses 17-24
95DMR6oenpU.one_line: Paradise's meticulous service and psychological peace, words for the unimaginable, the Quran's precision, and patience through Mecca's blows.
95DMR6oenpU.summary: Picking up at the description of Paradise, he argues its striking detail is the point: the service is perfected, down to the material of the cups and the exact measure poured, because attention to detail is how care is shown. He applies this to medicine, study, sport and business. The zanjabil cups and the spring named Salsabil show why the Quran uses unfamiliar words for Paradise: things no eye has seen cannot be described, just as a blind person cannot grasp colour, and we may receive senses we do not yet have. The eternal youths who serve are a separate creation, not deceased children. His favourite verse tells the reclining believer to look up and see bliss and a vast dominion: the psychological peace without which luxury means nothing, as any father on a ruined family holiday knows. Green silk, silver and a purifying drink, linked to the Prophet's basin, create calm. Allah then says their effort is appreciated, so no one feels like an impostor. Verse 23 ties the precision of Paradise to the precise sending down of the Quran. Verse 24 told the Prophet, amid Mecca's relentless blows, to be patient for his Lord's ruling and not follow the sinful or ungrateful.

outline.heading: Opening
A surah for those who want to hear of reward
outline.gist: Some people shy away from passages on punishment and death; Al-Insan is all reward. It holds one of the longest, most detailed descriptions of Paradise in the Quran, with only one other passage coming close.

outline.heading: Three dawah surahs, three proportions
outline.gist: Each of the three surahs carries logic, reward and punishment in different proportions: Al-Insan is mostly reward, Al-Mursalat mostly punishment. Remove any of the three and the equation fails to convince.

outline.heading: Each listener's build, and the Friday Fajr choice
outline.gist: Every person is moved more by one narrative, so the Quran provides all three. Of the three, Allah chose Al-Insan for the start of every week, alongside As-Sajdah's lovers of Allah who cannot stay in their beds.

outline.heading: Recap: reclining, perfect weather, fruit and cups
outline.gist: They recline with neither scorching sun nor cold, since rest needs the right weather; shade and humbled fruit come to them, and servants circulate with silver and crystal cups.

outline.heading: Service done exactly right
outline.gist: Cups are filled to the measure you want, not more or less. Unlike the restaurant that brings the wrong order, here every vessel is of the best quality and every order is right.

outline.heading: You spent your life serving; now you are served
outline.gist: You served Allah, His people, your family, your community, the sick and the poor, so now relax and recline while everything comes to you at a glance.

outline.heading: Your quality of work is your attention to detail
outline.gist: A lesson for anyone who will run a business. As a physician, his only real value is attention to subtle findings and listening deeply to patients' stories.

outline.heading: Restaurants and the 90 versus 99 student
outline.gist: Diners judge every detail, and the detail-oriented owner makes money, though it is exhausting. The gap between a 90 and a 99 is meticulousness.

outline.heading: Platini and the yard and a half
outline.gist: Champions and good athletes train alike; the difference is detail. He once heard Michel Platini instruct players down to standing a yard and a half from an opponent who favours one foot, which is why such teams win trophies.

outline.heading: He would not notice the new couch
outline.gist: The verses specify pure silver and crystal made with silver, details he admits he would never notice, as with the new couch his wife pointed out. They tell you that you are not coming to a mediocre place.

outline.heading: Detail shows care: the vendor and the barber
outline.gist: Attending to details shows people they are cared for: the vendor who works out your needs within your budget, the barber who cares how you look, earns your return. Allah promises to cater to every need with that depth.

outline.heading: Cups mixed with ginger
outline.gist: He recites verses 17 to 22. Zanjabil, ginger, was an Arab delicacy added to wine; the wine of Paradise brings none of this world's addiction, prison or liver disease.

outline.heading: Salsabil: a name from no known language
outline.gist: The ginger flows from a spring called Salsabil, one of the rare words in the Quran that belongs to no language, for a reason: Paradise holds what no eye has seen, no ear has heard and no heart has imagined.

outline.heading: Words only work for what we have seen, heard or imagined
outline.gist: A word for something beyond all three is gibberish to us. Sexuality cannot be explained to a six-year-old, nor colour to someone born blind.

outline.heading: Senses we do not yet have
outline.gist: We explore the universe with a handful of senses; who said those are all we will have in Paradise? So He drops unfamiliar words here and there to remind us we will grow beyond our little boxes, and only He knows what they mean.

outline.heading: Eternal youths like scattered pearls
outline.gist: They are created in Paradise for service, as angels are created for tasks, not the children of believers or disbelievers who died. Youth means quick, eager service, and seen moving about they look like scattered pearls.

outline.heading: His favourite verse: thamma means there
outline.gist: Thamma is not thumma, 'then', but 'there': what is present around you.

outline.heading: Look up: bliss and a great dominion
outline.gist: After the close-up details of couch, weather, fruit and cups, raise your head: as far as the eye can see there is bliss and a vast dominion, not the walls or horizon that end our sight here.

outline.heading: The ruined luxury holiday
outline.gist: Bliss needs its psychological components. A father who pays for the best restaurant and hotel can still find his wife silent, the children crying and the whole trip miserable, because peace inside matters more than food and drink.

outline.heading: Psychological bliss is what matters
outline.gist: Look around: there is room and enough for everyone, nothing to fight over, no worry about the next meal, disease, the next paycheque or tomorrow.

outline.heading: Green silk, light and heavy
outline.gist: Upon them, covering them from head down, are garments of green: light silk, sundus, and heavy silk, istabraq, to keep on or take off as they choose.

outline.heading: Persian words: Paradise is for everyone
outline.gist: Istabraq is a Persian word. Non-Arabic words in the Quran usually describe Paradise, because it is universal and not built to cater to Arabs alone.

outline.heading: Green: the most relaxing colour
outline.gist: Psychologists agree green relaxes, which is why hospital wards use green and blue; red and white stimulate and black brings fear. Green signals growth and food, blue water. They also wear silver bracelets, men and women alike.

outline.heading: A pure, purifying drink: the Prophet's basin
outline.gist: Sharaban tahura is pure in itself and purifies the one who drinks it. Scholars link it to the Prophet's basin, after which one never hungers or thirsts again.

outline.heading: Why silver, not gold
outline.gist: Asked why silver and not gold: gold is bright and loud and comes in more dynamic passages, while Al-Insan's bliss is calm, so even its vessels and jewellery are quiet.

outline.heading: No hunger, thirst, illness or death
outline.gist: After drinking from the Prophet's hand you never hunger, thirst, need the toilet, fall ill or die: the features that make this life what it is are removed.

outline.heading: Your effort is appreciated
outline.gist: They are told this is their reward and their striving is appreciated. Technically we did nothing to deserve it, but Allah stresses it so no one feels they got there undeservedly.

outline.heading: No impostor in Paradise
outline.gist: Feeling you are somewhere by a glitch breeds an inferiority complex and overcompensation, like impostor syndrome in high achievers. A little self-questioning is healthy, but Allah removes it in Paradise by His generosity.

outline.heading: Reciting the surah's final passage
outline.gist: With the descriptions done, he recites the closing section of the surah.

outline.heading: Interlude
Tanzila: sent down properly, by Allah alone
outline.gist: No other creature took part; the Quran came piece by piece, exactly when and how it should. A verb's root repeated at the end of a sentence stresses the act was done properly: as Paradise's service is meticulous, so was the revelation.

outline.heading: No other word would work
outline.gist: Any scholar of the Quran will show that changing a word would change the meaning, rhythm, tone and theme of the verse; every word is the only right one.

outline.heading: Be patient for your Lord's ruling: no end in sight
outline.gist: These were the Makkan years with no state, no safety for his followers, companions sent to Abyssinia, and no light at the end of the tunnel.

outline.heading: Makkah, a series of blows
outline.gist: The Makkan period was one blow after another to see how many he could take. These verses got him and the companions up each time, until the ruling came and other tribes offered support.

outline.heading: Revealed amid persecution; do not follow the sinful or ungrateful
outline.gist: Some scholars place the surah during the boycott of Banu Hashim, when there was no hope in sight. Do not walk in the footsteps of the sinful or the ungrateful.

outline.heading: Outro

56:83.en: Why, then, when (the soul) cometh up to the throat (of the dying)

56:84.en: And ye are at that moment looking

56:85.ar: وَنَحۡنُ أَقۡرَبُ إِلَيۡهِ مِنكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُبۡصِرُونَ
56:85.en: And We are nearer unto him than ye are, but ye see not

56:86.en: Why then, if ye are not in bondage (unto Us)

56:87.en: Do ye not force it back, if ye are truthful

75:26.en: Nay, but when the life cometh up to the throat

75:27.en: And men say: Where is the wizard (who can save him now)

75:28.en: And he knoweth that it is the parting

75:29.en: And agony is heaped on agony

6:93.ar: وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا أَوۡ قَالَ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ وَلَمۡ يُوحَ إِلَيۡهِ شَيۡءࣱ وَمَن قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثۡلَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُۗ وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ فِي غَمَرَٰتِ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ بَاسِطُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ أَخۡرِجُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمُۖ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَوۡنَ عَذَابَ ٱلۡهُونِ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَكُنتُمۡ عَنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ تَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ
6:93.en: Who is guilty of more wrong than he who forgeth a lie against Allah, or saith: I am inspired, when he is not inspired in aught; and who saith: I will reveal the like of that which Allah hath revealed? If thou couldst see, when the wrong-doers reach the pangs of death and the angels stretch their hands out (saying): Deliver up your souls. This day ye are awarded doom of degradation for that ye spake concerning Allah other than the truth, and used to scorn His portents

83:18.ar: كَلَّآ إِنَّ كِتَٰبَ ٱلۡأَبۡرَارِ لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ
83:18.en: Nay, but the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyin

7:40.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ عَنۡهَا لَا تُفَتَّحُ لَهُمۡ أَبۡوَٰبُ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَا يَدۡخُلُونَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ حَتَّىٰ يَلِجَ ٱلۡجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ ٱلۡخِيَاطِۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ

2:132.ar: وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَآ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعۡقُوبُ يَٰبَنِيَّ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰ لَكُمُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ
2:132.en: The same did Abraham enjoin upon his sons, and also Jacob, (saying): O my sons! Lo! Allah hath chosen for you the (true) religion; therefore die not save as men who have surrendered (unto Him)

2:133.ar: أَمۡ كُنتُمۡ شُهَدَآءَ إِذۡ حَضَرَ يَعۡقُوبَ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ إِذۡ قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِيۖ قَالُواْ نَعۡبُدُ إِلَٰهَكَ وَإِلَٰهَ ءَابَآئِكَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ إِلَٰهࣰ ا وَٰحِدࣰ ا وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
2:133.en: Or were ye present when death came to Jacob, when he said unto his sons: What will ye worship after me? They said: We shall worship thy god, the god of thy fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac, One Allah, and unto Him we have surrendered

l7iyJ2vCm-c.speaker: adnan
l7iyJ2vCm-c.speaker_note: continues his own Tazkiyah mortality series
l7iyJ2vCm-c.title: Tazkiyah Halaqa: Mortality, Episode 29
l7iyJ2vCm-c.one_line: Linking mortality to accountability: deeds are judged by their endings, so the believer's concern shifts from death itself to dying well.
l7iyJ2vCm-c.summary: He connects accepting mortality with accepting accountability. People fail to accept mortality either because they fear nothingness or because they see no hope in facing Allah. The bridge is the good ending: deeds are judged by how they conclude, so a life of sin can be redeemed at the end and a good start can be lost. He uses a wounded Olympic runner who finished long after the medals were given to show the race is about finishing. Not knowing our time is a mercy; knowing it would leave the nafs untamed until the final week. He tells of the man who killed a hundred people yet died repenting, the deathbeds of the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali and Bilal, and a man who could only recite a lustful verse at death because of an unrepented sin. Since you die as you live, filling most of your time with good deeds makes dying in one more likely. Endings also cure arrogance, because the whistle has not blown for anyone. He then narrates the long hadith of al-Bara' on the soul's departure, ascent, grave and companion of deeds for both the righteous and the wicked, urges people to witness deaths and washing, and closes by asking whether the shahadah fills them right now.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: acceptance clears away pettiness
outline.gist: Once past the initial sadness, accepting mortality removes petty problems and lets you focus on what matters; tell yourself the truth, not the nafs' lie.

outline.heading: Two lies, and death versus mortality
outline.gist: 'I have plenty of time' and 'I will die tonight' are both false, the second even pathological; mortality is a concept that grants clarity.

outline.heading: Why people fail to accept mortality
outline.gist: Either they fear nothingness, an atheist's fear, or they fear accountability so much they see no hope and ignore it.

outline.heading: The good ending (husn al-khatimah)
outline.gist: A frequent dua of the Prophet; things are judged by how they end, not how they begin, which is a healthy fear.

outline.heading: A good end can redeem a bad life, and the reverse
outline.gist: A life of sin ended in closeness to Allah outweighs what came before, while a strong start tanked at the end is lost.

outline.heading: The injured Olympic runner
outline.gist: Finishing an hour after the medals were awarded, he said he was sent to finish the race, not start it.

outline.heading: Make sure you are in a good position right now
outline.gist: Not obsessing over the past but being ready if taken now; a hard diagnosis gives warning to repent and set things right.

outline.heading: Refuge from sudden death
outline.gist: The Prophet sought refuge from a death with no time to repair ties or return rights; knowing your exact time would be the worst outcome.

outline.heading: Why Allah hid the time of death
outline.gist: If the nafs knew its date, nothing could tame it until a last-minute Hajj and repentance; hiding it aids self-purification.

outline.heading: Deeds are judged by their endings
outline.gist: Alongside intention, endings decide; this gives hope to anyone who changes now and holds on.

outline.heading: The man who killed a hundred
outline.gist: Told by a scholar he could repent and must leave his land, he died on the way; the angels disputed and the land was measured in his favour.

outline.heading: The Prophet's and Abu Bakr's deaths
outline.gist: The Prophet died asking for the highest companion; Abu Bakr asked to be shrouded in his old clothes since the living deserve the new.

outline.heading: Umar's and Uthman's deaths
outline.gist: Stabbed in the Prophet's mosque, Umar rebuked praise and asked for his face on the ground; Uthman died reading the mushaf rather than shed Muslim blood.

outline.heading: Ali's and Bilal's deaths
outline.gist: Ali asked that his killer be treated fairly and killed quickly if he died; Bilal rejoiced at meeting the Prophet and his companions.

outline.heading: The man who died reciting a lustful verse
outline.gist: Unable to say the shahadah, he repeated a line about a woman asking the way to a bathhouse, recalling an assault he regretted only failing to complete.

outline.heading: Saying 'la ilaha illallah' at the end
outline.gist: Being able to say it and repent in one's final moments is the greatest blessing and the sum of how one lived.

outline.heading: The real danger of sin
outline.gist: You do not know whether you will be given time to repent before being taken.

outline.heading: You die as you live
outline.gist: Allah commands us to die only as Muslims, and we control how we die by how we live; illness before death can be a chance to be purified.

outline.heading: Concern for the last moments replaces fear of death
outline.gist: Dying in the right state is better than a longer life that ends badly.

outline.heading: The praised fighter who was in the Fire
outline.gist: Companions praised a man killed in battle, but the Prophet said he was in Hell; he had taken his own life at the end.

outline.heading: Endings cure arrogance
outline.gist: The referee has not blown the whistle, so no one can keep score or judge themselves better than others.

outline.heading: The decree overtakes: you cannot fake it to the end
outline.gist: Some do the deeds of Paradise and end in Hell and vice versa; Allah exposes pretence and rescues hidden goodness in those raised in harm.

outline.heading: Do not judge how others ended
outline.gist: Some endings look clearly good, such as Muhammad al-Ghazali dying mid-lecture or people dying in sujud, but we take lessons without judging.

outline.heading: Why we keep striving
outline.gist: We fear Allah opening a door of temptation near the end; aim for your last deeds to be strongest, your last words kindest, your last worship purest.

outline.heading: Focus on the ending as a sign of acceptance
outline.gist: Endless stories exist of good and bad endings; focusing on yours reflects real acceptance of mortality.

outline.heading: The simple logic of probability
outline.gist: You are most likely to die doing what fills most of your time, so fill it with good deeds done for Allah.

outline.heading: When the soul reaches the throat
outline.gist: Allah describes onlookers around the dying while His angels are closer, and challenges deniers to bring the soul back.

outline.heading: When it reaches the collarbones
outline.gist: The dying person knows it is parting, legs come together in pain, and the drive is to his Lord.

outline.heading: The Prophet at the graveside
outline.gist: At a funeral he poked the soil in silence, then thrice sought refuge from the punishment of the grave before the longest description of death.

outline.heading: Angels of light come for the righteous
outline.gist: Angels with sun-like faces bring a shroud and perfume from Paradise and sit as far as he can see.

outline.heading: Witness death in person
outline.gist: Be present when elders pass and at washing, shrouding and burial; until then death is only theory, and the angel of death comes however one dies.

outline.heading: The good soul leaves like a drop of water
outline.gist: Called out to Allah's mercy and pleasure, it flows out like a drop from a spout with a moment's hesitation.

outline.heading: The pangs of death
outline.gist: Death is painful for everyone, but understood correctly its pain motivates and tames the nafs.

outline.heading: Don't be fooled by beginnings
outline.gist: The angels take the soul within a blink, wrap it in the perfume of Paradise and ascend.

outline.heading: Ascent through the heavens to Illiyyin
outline.gist: Each sky asks about the fragrance and welcomes him by his best-loved name; Allah records him among the highest and returns him to earth.

outline.heading: The believer's grave opens wide
outline.gist: The grave widens as far as he can see; he is shown his place in Hell had he chosen otherwise before that door closes forever.

outline.heading: Good deeds as companion in the grave
outline.gist: A handsome, fragrant man introduces himself as his good deeds and keeps him company as he longs for Paradise.

outline.heading: The wicked soul is torn out
outline.gist: Dark angels bring coarse cloth; the soul flees into the body and is dragged out like wet wool pulled over thorns.

outline.heading: Taken in humiliation
outline.gist: The Quran describes angels taking such souls in disgrace, wrapping them in fabric from Hell.

outline.heading: Refused at the heavens, recorded in Sijjin
outline.gist: The skies ask about the stench and call him by his most hated name; he is refused entry and recorded in the lowest register.

outline.heading: The grave closes in
outline.gist: He is thrown into a grave that constricts until his bones interlock; he is shown his lost place in Paradise and its door is closed.

outline.heading: Bad deeds as companion
outline.gist: An ugly, foul-smelling man is his bad deeds; he begs Allah not to establish the Hour because what awaits is worse.

outline.heading: Live as if this is the last stretch of the race
outline.gist: Shift focus from the pain of death and leaving people to ensuring the last few years are your best with Allah.

outline.heading: Meeting a Lord who rejoices
outline.gist: In another narration Allah laughs to the righteous servant who arrives longing to meet Him.

outline.heading: The Muslim mindset at death is unique
outline.gist: Unlike most of humanity, the believer's concern at death is his last state, as with Ya'qub asking his sons what they would worship.

outline.heading: Ibrahim and Ya'qub's final counsel
outline.gist: Both told their children Allah chose this deen for them, so do not die except as Muslims.

outline.heading: Transitions always hurt
outline.gist: Like moving to a better job or city, leaving the familiar is painful even when what lies ahead is better.

outline.heading: Last words as the key to Paradise
outline.gist: Whoever's last words are la ilaha illallah enters Paradise, but never use this to judge others.

outline.heading: Are you filled with it now?
outline.gist: If your last breath came at the door tonight, would the shahadah be what you love most? If not, work until it is.

outline.heading: Umar's relief at his killer
outline.gist: Umar praised Allah that his killer was not a Muslim, hoping to die as a martyr; that focus on the ending is open to all.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Not knowing anyone's ending removes grounds for arrogance and judging others.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The detailed journey of righteous and wicked souls from death through the grave.

themes.label: Visiting the sick, caring for elders and the vulnerable

quran.point: Do not die except as Muslims.

When it reaches the collarbones and leg is wrapped with leg, the drive is to your Lord.
Angels extend their hands to take the souls of wrongdoers in humiliation.
From the earth We created you, into it We return you and from it We bring you out again.
The record of the righteous is in Illiyyin.
The record of the wicked is in Sijjin.
The gates of heaven are not opened for those who denied.
Ibrahim and Ya'qub counselled their sons to die only in submission and asked what they would worship after them.

hadith.gist: The Prophet sought refuge in Allah from a sudden death.
Deeds are judged by their endings.
A man who killed ninety-nine, then a hundred, was told he could repent and must leave his land; he died on the way and the angels of mercy took him.
The Prophet died asking for the highest companion.
A man praised for fighting bravely was said to be in Hell; he later took his own life.
One of you does the deeds of the people of Paradise until only an arm's length remains, then what is written overtakes him, and the reverse.
The long narration of al-Bara' ibn Azib describing the departure, ascent and grave of the believing and the disbelieving soul.
Allah laughs to the servant who comes to Him, in joy at meeting him.

maxims: Judged by how it ended, not how it began
You die how you live
The referee has not blown the whistle
Allah won't let you fake it till the end
Don't be fooled by beginnings, look at the ends

stories.point: He was sent to finish the race, not to start it; life is about how you finish.

stories.who: The man who killed a hundred people
stories.point: Repentance remains open, and dying while turning back gives hope.

stories.who: Deaths of the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali and Bilal
stories.point: Their final moments show humility, fear of accountability and joy at meeting Allah.

stories.who: A shopkeeper who could only recite a lustful verse at death

Died while speaking about Allah, an example of a visibly good ending.

takeaways: Make dua often for a good ending
Repent promptly, since you may not be given time later
Fill most of your time with good deeds so you are likely to die in one
Witness a death, washing and burial to make mortality real
Make the shahadah the word you love most now, not only at the end

24:47.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلرَّسُولِ وَأَطَعۡنَا ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّىٰ فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَۚ وَمَآ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
24:47.en: And they say: We believe in Allah and the messenger, and we obey; then after that a faction of them turn away. Such are not believers

24:48.ar: وَإِذَا دُعُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ لِيَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ إِذَا فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُم مُّعۡرِضُونَ
24:48.en: And when they appeal unto Allah and His messenger to judge between them, lo! a faction of them are averse

24:49.ar: وَإِن يَكُن لَّهُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ يَأۡتُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِ مُذۡعِنِينَ
24:49.en: But if right had been with them they would have come unto him willingly

24:50.ar: أَفِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ أَمِ ٱرۡتَابُوٓاْ أَمۡ يَخَافُونَ أَن يَحِيفَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَرَسُولُهُۥۚ بَلۡ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
24:50.en: Is there in their hearts a disease, or have they doubts, or fear they lest Allah and His messenger should wrong them in judgment? Nay, but such are evil-doers

24:51.ar: إِنَّمَا كَانَ قَوۡلَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ إِذَا دُعُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ لِيَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ أَن يَقُولُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَأَطَعۡنَاۚ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
24:51.en: The saying of (all true) believers when they appeal unto Allah and His messenger to judge between them is only that they say: We hear and we obey. And such are the successful

24:52.ar: وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَيَخۡشَ ٱللَّهَ وَيَتَّقۡهِ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَآئِزُونَ
24:52.en: He who obeyeth Allah and His messenger, and feareth Allah, and keepeth duty (unto Him): such indeed are the victorious

24:53.ar: ۞وَأَقۡسَمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ جَهۡدَ أَيۡمَٰنِهِمۡ لَئِنۡ أَمَرۡتَهُمۡ لَيَخۡرُجُنَّۖ قُل لَّا تُقۡسِمُواْۖ طَاعَةࣱ مَّعۡرُوفَةٌۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
24:53.en: They swear by Allah solemnly that, if thou order them, they will go forth. Say: Swear not; known obedience (is better). Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do

24:54.ar: قُلۡ أَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱلرَّسُولَۖ فَإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيۡهِ مَا حُمِّلَ وَعَلَيۡكُم مَّا حُمِّلۡتُمۡۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُوهُ تَهۡتَدُواْۚ وَمَا عَلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ إِلَّا ٱلۡبَلَٰغُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
24:54.en: Say: Obey Allah and obey the messenger. But if ye turn away, then (it is) for him (to do) only that wherewith he hath been charged, and for you (to do) only that wherewith ye have been charged. If ye obey him, ye will go aright. But the messenger hath no other charge than to convey (the message) plainly

31:20.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَسۡبَغَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعَمَهُۥ ظَٰهِرَةࣰ وَبَاطِنَةࣰۗ وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِي ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲ وَلَا هُدࣰ ى وَلَا كِتَٰبࣲ مُّنِيرࣲ‏
31:20.en: See ye not how Allah hath made serviceable unto you whatsoever is in the skies and whatsoever is in the earth and hath loaded you with His favours both without and within? Yet of mankind is he who disputeth concerning Allah, without knowledge or guidance or a scripture giving light

24:55.ar: وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَيَسۡتَخۡلِفَنَّهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ كَمَا ٱسۡتَخۡلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمۡ دِينَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي ٱرۡتَضَىٰ لَهُمۡ وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ خَوۡفِهِمۡ أَمۡنࣰ اۚ يَعۡبُدُونَنِي لَا يُشۡرِكُونَ بِي شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
24:55.en: Allah hath promised such of you as believe and do good work that He will surely make them to succeed (the present rulers) in the earth even as He caused those who were before them to succeed (others); and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He hath approved for them, and will give them in exchange safety after their fear. They serve Me. They ascribe no thing as partner unto Me. Those who disbelieve henceforth, they are the miscreants

24:56.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱلرَّسُولَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
24:56.en: Establish worship and pay the poor-due and obey the messenger, that haply ye may find mercy

24:57.ar: لَا تَحۡسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مُعۡجِزِينَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَمَأۡوَىٰهُمُ ٱلنَّارُۖ وَلَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
24:57.en: Think not that the disbelievers can escape in the land. Fire will be their home - a hapless journey's end

IGsFouKhL6M.title: Listening to the Divine: An-Nur 54-57
IGsFouKhL6M.one_line: What are the unique responsibilities of Muslims in the West? Advocacy and real obedience, not oaths; the proven promise of 24:55.
IGsFouKhL6M.summary: This khutbah on An-Nur 47-57, a month before Ramadan, asks Muslims in the West one question: what are your unique responsibilities? He surveys an ummah in turmoil, Gaza still bleeding with less media noise, Syria, Sudan and Yemen, and contrasts it with Muslims in Canada who prosper and enjoy more freedom to speak than anywhere on earth, a freedom that lasts only if preserved through advocacy. Responsibilities differ by where and when you live, so beyond the shared duties of prayer, fasting and zakat there are communal obligations, and he has been asking for twelve years what ours are without an echo. He names advocacy, educating youth to carry the ummah, voicing the voiceless and pushing policy toward justice, and confesses that his Syrian upbringing taught him to keep his head down, which he now thinks was probably wrong; he asks the youth not to follow their parents on that. Judgment is individual because each person's hand is different; a mother of seven in Sudan will not be asked your questions. The verses describe people who swear they would sacrifice everything yet turn away from simple rulings; Allah wants known obedience, not oaths. He ends with the proven promise of 24:55: security and establishment for those who do their part.

outline.heading: Opening
Recitation of 24:47
outline.gist: They say we believe in Allah and the Messenger and we obey, then a party of them turns away; those are not believers.

outline.heading: The month before Ramadan: our lowest point
outline.gist: The month before Ramadan is when we are farthest away, having used up our spiritual momentum; fast and pray more now so we arrive with something to offer.

outline.heading: An ummah in turmoil, and our share of it
outline.gist: Gaza still bleeds, only more quietly in the media, alongside Syria, Sudan and parts of Yemen. Muslims in the West carry a significant responsibility toward them, because Islam cannot be understood any other way.

outline.heading: We do well here, and freedom lasts only if preserved
outline.gist: We are one body. Muslims in Canada do well socially, financially and academically, and he has more freedom to pray and speak here than almost anywhere on earth, so far. It continues only if we preserve it, and part of that is advocacy for ourselves and for Muslims elsewhere.

outline.heading: The off-grid fantasy: not yet
outline.gist: He feels daily the urge to move far away with a few chickens and goats and no internet, but a Muslim is not offered that option yet. The Prophet described a time when taking your sheep to the mountains would be the only way to survive; this is not it. Contribution, participation and advocacy are what we carry here.

outline.heading: Responsibilities differ by circumstance
outline.gist: What you carry depends on where and when you live, your expertise, age, gender, origin and wealth. Beyond the individual duties every Muslim shares, such as prayer, fasting and zakat, there are communal obligations.

outline.heading: Is your shoulder under the load?
outline.gist: He has no authority to tell you your unique responsibilities, only to ask what they are. Are you carrying the burden or walking alongside with your hand on it, pretending?

outline.heading: Twelve years asking, no echo
outline.gist: It is our duty to know what we are required to do as Muslims in the West. He has asked this for twelve years and nothing comes back; standing here and speaking is his job, so what is yours?

outline.heading: If you want a different future
outline.gist: If you do not want more meaningless bloodshed, persecution, double standards, a world run by the law of the jungle and a planet fried beyond living, identify the responsibilities you carry.

outline.heading: What we carry: advocacy, youth, the voiceless, policy
outline.gist: Muslims in the West carry advocacy for others, educating youth to carry the ummah, being the voice of those who have none, and pushing national and foreign policy toward justice.

outline.heading: Standing on our own two feet
outline.gist: The Prime Minister's speech last week used big words, hard to carry out and perhaps years late. As Muslim Canadians, do we understand what it means to take responsibility for our values and see them echoed in how the country runs and what it says abroad, or will we keep our heads down?

outline.heading: Head down in Syria: probably wrong
outline.gist: He lived most of his life keeping his head down in Syria, doing good quietly and not rocking the boat, and thought it right. After all the bloodshed his people saw, he thinks it was probably wrong.

outline.heading: Don't follow us on that one
outline.gist: Many young people hear their parents urge a low profile; the parents mean well but know nothing else. He asks the youth not to inherit it: voice concerns, get involved, bring the challenge forward and push it so justice can occur.

outline.heading: Judged alone by the hand you were dealt
outline.gist: A mother of seven in Sudan will not be held to your standard. There is no bingo-card judgment: each comes before the Lord alone and concealed, accountable for his own opportunities and challenges. So what burden beyond the basics is unique to you?

outline.heading: Turning away unless the ruling favours them
outline.gist: 24:47-50: they say they believe and obey, then turn away when called to Allah's judgment and come running only when the right is theirs; is there disease in their hearts, or do they fear injustice? They are the wrongdoers.

outline.heading: We hear and we obey
outline.gist: 24:51-52: when the believers are called to Allah and His Messenger they say we hear and we obey; whoever obeys and fears Allah is the successful.

outline.heading: Do not swear: known obedience
outline.gist: 24:53: they swear their strongest oaths that they would go out if commanded, yet will not follow simple rulings. Say: do not swear; what counts is known obedience.

outline.heading: Obey Allah and the Messenger
outline.gist: 24:54: if you turn away, he bears what he was charged with and you bear yours; obey him and you are guided, and his duty is only clear conveyance.

outline.heading: Interlude
Who will not give a little will never give much
outline.gist: In Arabic: whoever disobeys Allah in small daily rulings will never sacrifice life or wealth. Their oaths are empty talk; even a thief swears readily when asked. The only oath that matters is obedience.

outline.heading: Minus fourteen, from the car to the door
outline.gist: None of us here is asked to give his life or all his wealth. We live in peace and comfort: at minus fourteen people elsewhere would die of cold, while we feel it only from car to door, because Allah has lavished His blessings on us.

outline.heading: Carry Islam's concern or it carries yours
outline.gist: We cannot compare our lives with those whose children are killed and who find a bullet instead of bread. Each of us must carry a share of Islam's concern; if you do not carry it, Islam carries you. Have you reflected on what yours is?

outline.heading: Your questions will not be a Gazan father's
outline.gist: Do not think the questions put to the father of a child killed in Gaza or a widow raising orphans will be the ones put to you; he fears for himself and for us.

outline.heading: The promise of 24:55
outline.gist: Such behaviour is not welcome. Then the promise: Allah will give those who believe and do good stewardship of the earth as He gave those before, establish the religion He chose for them and replace their fear with security, as long as they worship Him alone.

outline.heading: Do your part; they are not invincible
outline.gist: 24:56-57: establish prayer, give zakat and obey the Messenger to find mercy; the disbelievers are not invincible on earth and their refuge is the fire. Know your responsibilities and carry them.

outline.heading: A proven ayah
outline.gist: He does not ask for blind belief: the promise was proven in the Prophet's life and repeatedly through history, and will happen again if we understand what Allah asks and commit to it.

outline.heading: Outro
